function pairs(args, allowed, switches = []) {
  const values = new Map();
  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index++) {
    const key = args[index];
    if (!allowed.includes(key) && !switches.includes(key) || values.has(key)) throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Unknown or repeated option: ' + key);
    if (switches.includes(key)) { values.set(key, true); continue; }
    const value = args[++index];
    if (!value || value.startsWith('--')) throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Missing value for ' + key);
    values.set(key, value);
  }
  return values;
}
function portNumber(value, fallback) {
  if (value === undefined) return fallback;
  if (!/^\d{1,5}$/.test(String(value)) || Number(value) > 65535) throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Port must be 0–65535.');
  return Number(value);
}
export async function startMerchantMcp({ configPath, port = 3211, tokenEnv = 'MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN',
  environment = process.env, stellarExpertFetchImpl, woocommerceFetchImpl, mppFetchImpl, oauthConfigPath, oauthFetchImpl, accounting, consoleDirectory, consoleBinding, providerOptions = {} } = {}) {
  if (!configPath || !/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/.test(tokenEnv)) throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Supply a merchant configuration and token environment-variable name.');
  const providerPrototype = providerOptions && typeof providerOptions === 'object' ? Object.getPrototypeOf(providerOptions) : undefined;
  if (providerPrototype !== Object.prototype && providerPrototype !== null)
    throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Supply a plain providerOptions object for trusted native startup.');
  port = portNumber(port, 3211);
  const operator = await openMerchantOperator(configPath,
    { environment, stellarExpert: { environment, fetchImpl: stellarExpertFetchImpl }, woocommerce: { environment, fetchImpl: woocommerceFetchImpl }, mpp: { environment, fetchImpl: mppFetchImpl }, opensearch: { environment }, opencage: { env: environment }, grpc: { environment }, openapi: { environment }, arcgis: { environment }, opendatasoft: { environment }, accounting: { ...accounting, environment }, ...providerOptions });
  let server, access, operatorConsole, draining=false;
  try {
    access = await loadOAuthResourceHost({configPath:oauthConfigPath ?? environment.MCP_OAUTH_CONFIG,
      bearerToken:environment[tokenEnv],fetchImpl:oauthFetchImpl});
    const handler = createMcpToolHandler(operator, { ...access.transportOptions, maxRequestBytes: operator.maxRequestBytes,
      allowedClientOrigins: String(environment.MCP_CLIENT_ORIGINS ?? '').split(',').map(value => value.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      serverName: 'starforge-merchant-operator', serverVersion: '0.1.0',
      instructions: merchantInstructions(operator.tools) });
    if (consoleBinding !== undefined && consoleDirectory === undefined)
      throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'A managed console binding requires its original console directory.');
    if(consoleDirectory!==undefined){
      if(typeof consoleDirectory!=='string'||!consoleDirectory)throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR','Supply a private operator console directory.');
      operatorConsole=await (await import('./console/service.mjs')).createMerchantConsole({
        operator,configPath,directory:consoleDirectory,...access.transportOptions,binding:consoleBinding});
    }
    const routed=operatorConsole?async(req,res)=>{
      try{
        if(draining){
          res.writeHead(503,{'content-type':'application/json','cache-control':'no-store'});
          res.end(JSON.stringify({error:{code:'OPERATOR_CLOSING',message:'The original merchant host is closing.'}}));return;
        }
        if(await operatorConsole.handler(req,res))return;
        await handler(req,res);
      }catch(error){
        if(res.headersSent){res.destroy(error);return;}
        res.writeHead(500,{'content-type':'application/json','cache-control':'no-store'});
        res.end(JSON.stringify({error:{code:error.code??'CONSOLE_ERROR',message:'The original operator could not return this response.'}}));
      }
    }:handler;
    server = createServer(access.wrap(routed));
    server.requestTimeout = 150000; server.headersTimeout = 10000; server.keepAliveTimeout = 2000;
    await new Promise((done, reject) => {
      server.once('error', reject);
      server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', () => { server.removeListener('error', reject); done(); });
    });
  } catch (error) {
    server?.close();
    try { await operatorConsole?.close(); } finally { try { await operator.close(); } finally { await access?.close(); } }
    throw error;
  }
  let closing, stopped;
  const close = () => {
    if (closing) return closing;
    draining=true;
    closing = (async () => {
      stopped??=new Promise((done, reject) => server.close(error => error&&error.code!=='ERR_SERVER_NOT_RUNNING' ? reject(error) : done()));
      // Preserve the original customer checkpoints, then let the native owners
      // cancel/drain accepted provider work before waiting for their returns.
      try {
        operatorConsole?.beginClose();
        const results=await Promise.allSettled([operatorConsole?.close(),operator.close()]);
        const errors=results.filter(value=>value.status==='rejected').map(value=>value.reason);
        if(errors.length)throw errors.length===1?errors[0]:Object.assign(new AggregateError(errors,'Original merchant shutdown is incomplete.'),{code:'OPERATOR_SHUTDOWN_INCOMPLETE'});
      } finally {
        try { await access.close(); }
        finally { server.closeAllConnections(); await stopped; }
      }
    })();
    closing.catch(()=>{closing=undefined;});
    return closing;
  };
  const url=new URL('http://127.0.0.1:' + server.address().port).origin;
  return { operator, server, url, maxRequestBytes: operator.maxRequestBytes, authorization:access.describe(),
    ...(operatorConsole?{consoleUrl:url+'/operator/',operatorConsole}:{}),close };
}
export async function main(args = process.argv.slice(2)) {
  if (!args.length || args.length === 1 && ['--help', 'help'].includes(args[0])) { process.stdout.write(HELP); return; }

# Analysis Dataset publication through native MCP

This extension connects the existing Analysis Dataset workflow to its original MCP host. It starts with a completed query export, saves an explicitly reviewed recipe, prepares the native package, and carries that same package through the configured Frictionless workbench and publisher. It also receives complete original package and source-export files through the maintained saved-file reader.

The implementation consists of three additions:

- `native-analysis-publication.mjs`: `createNativePublicationActions({reads, parse})`.
- `native-analysis-publication-schema.mjs`: `nativePublicationOperations`.
- This guide.

The existing `native-analysis.mjs` dispatcher supplies the selected workspace record, authenticated HTTP methods, cancellation, and original file reader. It owns shutdown and drains admitted work. The extension creates no additional service, per-request process, collector, reader lease, or publisher.

## Select an existing workspace and completed export

Use the existing native Analysis MCP workspace selection. The example bodies below are extension arguments after that selection; retain the outer workspace exactly as supplied by the maintained native Analysis tool.

Read `dataset-configuration` first. Its response identifies representations, configured publication connections, target workspace UUIDs, source actions and reads, file names, and limits. A connection URL can include an actual path. Preserve its complete URL and workspace UUID.

Native connection aliases follow `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}`. Recipe names use the separate grammar `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}`.

Page the original completed exports:

~~~json
{"operation":"dataset-exports","limit":25}
~~~

Retain `next_before` and continue until null. History replies explicitly identify themselves as metadata. They retain original IDs, counts, requests/results metadata and native state paths. A history projection is not a request body for replay.

Select an original export and review its source:

~~~json
{
  "operation":"dataset-review",
  "query_export_id":"<original Analysis hex32 export ID>",
  "manifest_sha256":"<original export manifest SHA-256>",
  "sample_rows":20
}
~~~

The review reads saved output without executing its SQL again. It binds the original workspace, export, manifest, source binding, row count, columns, and typed SQLite-scalar preview.

The native preview is bounded. If the complete reply exceeds the MCP envelope, the helper explicitly reports native/omitted preview rows, column count and original full-source availability. Each included scalar is unchanged. A preview is not a complete dataset, and omitted fields are not empty fields.

## Save the complete reviewed recipe

Choose the original native recipe through the existing Dataset review: source export/manifest, selected fields and order, representations, title/resource, and explicit source rights. The helper supplies no rights, authorization, or publisher approval.

Persist the complete request before dispatch:

~~~json
{
  "operation":"dataset-save-recipe",
  "id":"<retained Analysis hex32 recipe request ID>",
  "name":"<chosen recipe name>",
  "expected_revision":0,
  "recipe":{"...":"the complete reviewed native recipe"}
}
~~~

The shown recipe is a placeholder, not an executable minimal recipe. Use the actual native recipe schema and reviewed fields.

The native save reconciles an existing request before consulting changed source availability or the current name revision. The returned recipe is normalized by the original validator. Retain its `id`, `revision`, `recipe_sha256`, source binding, and your complete original request. The public recipe view does not expose its private request journal.

Use `dataset-recipe {recipe_id}` to reopen the saved recipe and current name-head metadata. A newer head does not change that historical recipe.

Prepare the package with a retained Analysis job ID:

~~~json
{
  "operation":"dataset-prepare",
  "id":"<retained Analysis hex32 package job ID>",
  "recipe_id":"<saved original recipe ID>",
  "recipe_sha256":"<saved normalized recipe SHA-256>"
}
~~~

The helper first reads `/api/jobs/<id>` and compares the complete original request. A saved `COMPLETE` result returns directly. Only the precise native `ANALYSIS_JOB_NOT_FOUND` outcome permits an initial POST. A network error, generic HTTP 404, authorization failure or invalid response does not establish absence.

For a non-complete existing job, the identical request goes to the original Analysis start/resume rules. The helper never chooses a replacement ID or resets its native job.

After a lost reply, read `dataset-job {id}` before continuing. An authoritative saved success survives a late cancellation.

## Inspect the package and exact download index

`dataset-package {id}` reads the native UI package view, including normalized recipe, field statistics, native projection conflicts, declared input, queries text and enriched index. Large views explicitly describe their metadata projection and original complete files.

The native package has six original files:

| File | Visibility | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `datapackage.json` | Public | Original package descriptor |
| `data.json` | Public | Complete selected resource data |
| `publication.zip` | Public | Complete package handover |
| `recipe.json` | Private | Normalized reviewed recipe |
| `manifest.json` | Private | Source, recipe and field evidence |
| `report.html` | Private | Native readable report |

Read its index:

~~~json
{"operation":"dataset-downloads","id":"<original package job ID>","offset":0,"limit":25}
~~~

The response has this exact structure:

~~~js
{
  workspaceId, jobId, source: false, indexSha256,
  indexFile: {
    filename: "downloads.json",
    bytes, sha256, contentType: "application/json"
  },
  fileCount, files,
  page: {offset, limit, total, nextOffset},
  binding
}
~~~

`files` contains unchanged original file records: name, relative name, bytes, SHA-256, MIME type and visibility. Continue `page.nextOffset` until null. The bounded binding retains native IDs, hashes, row count and column count; the raw index retains complete columns.

`indexSha256` hashes the original `downloads.json` bytes. It does not hash an enriched HTTP response, a reserialized object, or the paged MCP response. The helper reads the native view and exact raw index file, verifies the raw hash, and compares every required original index field before publishing its completed private cache record.

The raw index is intentionally absent from `index.files`, so its hash never recursively includes itself. Read it using `indexFile.filename` and `indexFile.sha256`.

## Read and continue unchanged file ranges

Choose the exact index and original file:

~~~json
{
  "operation":"dataset-file",
  "id":"<original package job ID>",
  "source":false,
  "index_sha256":"<original downloads.json SHA-256>",
  "filename":"publication.zip",
  "sha256":"<original publication.zip SHA-256>",
  "byteOffset":0,
  "maxBytes":65536
}
~~~

The wrapper preserves the original reader response:

~~~js
{
  workspaceId, jobId, source, indexSha256, filename,
  file: {
    contentType, bytes, sha256, byteOffset, returnedBytes,
    encoding: "base64", data, nextByteOffset,
    verifiedSavedFile: true
    // Original reader may include text for a complete valid UTF-8 file.
  }
}
~~~

Decode `data` at its acknowledged `byteOffset` and continue `nextByteOffset` until null. Keep the same file size and digest through interruption. The maintained typed retained-download client handles durable prefix hashing and final download publication when used by the operator.

The host cache lives inside its selected original native MCP workspace:

`analysis/dataset-files/<Analysis workspace ID>/<job ID>/<index SHA-256>/`

Only original IDs and fixed components select that path. The caller supplies no arbitrary local destination or source path. Native names such as `reviews/<UUID>.json` remain public file identities; payload cache paths use verified SHA-256 values.

Original initialization functions publish complete fsynced bytes and immutable records. The raw index is published before its completed record. A completed record with a missing raw index is an integrity error. Changed private mode, hash, type or saved bytes also remains an error. Only an absent cache object permits capture.

An absent individual file triggers a fresh check of the current native index and exact file identity before acquisition. Already captured files can reopen without the service even if later native history exposes a newer index. A newer live index cannot supply uncaptured bytes for an older saved selection.

The range limit is 65,536 bytes. Complete-file cache limit is 128 MiB per member; raw index limits are 20 MiB for package and 8 MiB for source. Larger output members remain visible and use the existing Python `dataset-download` streaming path. They are not silently omitted or allocated into this MCP cache.

The existing offline Python `DatasetPublication(directory, expected_index_sha256=...)` exposes `inspect()` and `file(name)`. Use the maintained Python `dataset-open` / `dataset-download` interface for complete streaming receiving.

## Carry the package through the original native source

Analysis recipe/package/source-command IDs are hex32. Native workbench request, capture, edition, review, publisher-run and export IDs are UUIDv4. Preserve those separate original identities.

Every source action retains the exact configured endpoint and actual native workspace UUID. Include the completed package and original index hash whenever the native action requires its selected bytes.

~~~json
{
  "operation":"dataset-source",
  "id":"<retained Analysis hex32 command ID>",
  "connection":"<original lowercase configured alias>",
  "action":"intake",
  "args":{
    "expectedVersion":"<actual native version>",
    "label":"<chosen label>"
  },
  "package_id":"<original package job ID>",
  "index_sha256":"<original downloads.json SHA-256>",
  "reviewed_endpoint":"<exact configured URL, including its path>",
  "expected_workspace_id":"<actual native UUIDv4>"
}
~~~

Replace the version placeholder with its actual native value and type. Arguments pass unchanged, including camelCase keys. Native validation owns each action, declared input alias, optimistic version, source hash and explicit review.

| Stage | Actions | Original state to retain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source intake | `open`, `intake`, `edition` | Configured input, current version, capture ID and chosen label |
| Reviewed selection | `review-edition`, `select`, `plan` | Edition/review IDs, reviewer/note, source hash and complete plan |
| Source handover | `export`, `download-export` | Original edition, selected review, original export request and source hash |
| Native continuation | `cancel`, `resume` | Original operation/request ID |
| Publisher preparation | `publisher-extract`, `publisher-review` | Original plan/run, candidate digest and explicit target review |
| Publisher completion | `publisher-publish`, `publisher-recover`, `publisher-cancel` | Original plan/run/review and accepted or uncertain outcome |

`dataset-source-read` exposes original reads: `status`, `input`, `current`, `request`, `capture`, `edition`, `review`, `plan-input`, `publisher-status`, `publisher-target`, `publisher-inspect` and `inspect-export`. It uses the same reviewed connection/package binding and exact arguments without a mutation ID. Its underlying HTTP POST remains a native read.

Before continuation, `dataset-source` reads the original Analysis job and compares `request.original_request` with the complete submitted body. Its native spec separately preserves target, package, arguments and the derived request UUID. An uncertain reply does not authorize a new ID or changed command.

An Analysis command can be `COMPLETE` while its native `result.operation.state` or `result.run.state` remains `RUNNING`. Read that same native operation/run until its actual outcome is known. Large tool responses keep explicit native state paths alongside metadata; the original complete response remains available through the service/files.

## Receive the native source export

After the original `download-export` command completes:

~~~json
{
  "operation":"dataset-downloads",
  "id":"<original download-export Analysis job ID>",
  "source":true,
  "offset":0,
  "limit":25
}
~~~

The source index binds original package/index, native workspace, export ID, source hash, and both native manifest identities. Files retain native sorted order, at most 10,000 records and 512 MiB total. Names are limited to `manifest.json`, `source.tar.gz`, `source-edition.json`, `capture-inspection.json`, `RECEIVING.md` and `reviews/<UUIDv4>.json`.

Its raw filename is `files-index.json`. Read that file and every selected member with `dataset-file`, preserving `source:true`, the same Analysis command, source-index SHA and member SHA. The original `manifest.json` must match `native_manifest_sha256`.

Receiving retains complete native source. The helper does not interpret exported text as instructions or execute the publisher again.

## Interruption and cancellation

| Observed outcome | Continue with |
| --- | --- |
| Recipe save reply lost | Same recipe ID and complete request; native replay precedes current head checks |
| Package/source reply lost | Original `dataset-job`, then identical request only when native resume permits |
| Original job read failed | Preserve the request; unavailable service does not prove job absence |
| Original job is `COMPLETE` | Saved authoritative result and its actual nested native state |
| Native workbench operation still runs | Original request/capture/edition reads or supported same-request resume |
| Publisher reply uncertain | Original run inspection and `publisher-recover` with unchanged plan/run/review |
| Cancellation requested | `dataset-cancel`, then original job read; accepted native work remains accepted |
| File reply lost | Same index/member and retained acknowledged offset |
| Service unavailable after capture | Existing exact cache and original reader, without a new native action |
| Saved hash, mode or type changed | Reconcile the saved source; do not overwrite it |
| Member exceeds 128 MiB | Original Python streaming downloader and exact same selection |

The only new retained state is the verified index/file cache. Job execution, source selections, reviews, native actions, publisher uncertainty, cancellation and portable workspace recovery remain with their existing products.

# Analysis Lineage through the native agent

This interface uses the existing Analysis workspace, its saved lineage plans and its original publication worker. An operator chooses a completed Analysis job, reviews its complete dependency closure, saves the exact event source, publishes that saved plan to a configured collector and downloads the original delivery files.

The agent receives configured aliases and original IDs. Startup connection files, producer credentials and local cache paths remain with the host. Review, plan saving and downloads do not publish events.

## Configure the existing hosts

Start the original Analysis service with its existing Lineage connections configuration and complete selected runtime. A connection names an original collector workspace UUID, startup connection file and optional private producer-token file. The service reads the current startup file; the reviewed collector origin remains pinned. The original bridge permits a local collector restart to change only the port on the same numeric loopback host and scheme.

Register that running Analysis service in the existing MCP native workspace. Use its actual Analysis alias as `analysisWorkspace`. Every operation below uses the original native Analysis envelope:

~~~json
{
  "action": "analysis",
  "analysisWorkspace": "analysis",
  "analysisOperation": "lineage-configuration",
  "analysisRequest": {}
}
~~~

The response is the existing native Analysis envelope; its `result` is the operation result described here. The configuration includes `workspace_id` for Analysis, `can_publish`, existing collector aliases, their actual collector UUIDs and current availability. It contains no token or startup-file path.

The identities have different roles:

| Field | Original identity |
|---|---|
| `analysisWorkspace` | Host-registered Analysis alias |
| Analysis `workspace_id` | 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters |
| `connection` | Existing collector alias from `lineage-configuration` |
| `expected_workspace_id` | Canonical hyphenated collector workspace UUID |
| `job_id` | Completed source Analysis job, 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters |
| Plan `id` / `plan_id` | Saved plan, 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters |
| Publication `id` | Original Analysis publication job, 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters |
| `operation_id` | Original collector idempotency key retained by the plan |
| `plan_sha256` / `index_sha256` | Exact reviewed plan / selected delivery index |

A publication request ID must be saved before dispatch and reused after a lost reply. The plan already owns the original collector idempotency key.

## Review and save a complete plan

Call `lineage-jobs` with `{}` or `{before, limit}`. These are completed imports, response imports, queries, complete query exports and workbooks supported by the original projection. Use the returned `next_before` unchanged.

Call `lineage-review` with the selected `job_id` and an explicit `include_sql` choice. SQL inclusion changes the retained source and its review digest. The default summary returns `snapshot_sha256`, `events_sha256`, `events_bytes` and the original job/dataset/event counts. It does not rerun Analysis.

The optional fields `collection`, `offset` and `limit` page metadata from the same complete source:

| Collection | Returned metadata |
|---|---|
| `summary` | Original digests, counts and bounded warning preview |
| `jobs` | Original job/run IDs, timestamps, dependency counts and native detail hashes |
| `datasets` | Native dataset names, namespaces, facet names and scalar Analysis metadata |
| `events` | Original event type/time, run/job identity and input/output counts |

`limit` defaults to 25 and is at most 100. `projection.next_offset` is the next position; a byte-bound page can return fewer than the requested limit. `projection.kind` is `metadata`. Large mappings, SQL text, document bodies and full facet content remain in the original complete download files. Warning previews and omitted metadata fields are marked explicitly.

Save the plan with `lineage-save-plan`:

~~~json
{
  "id": "<saved plan ID:32hex>",
  "job_id": "<original completed Analysis job ID:32hex>",
  "expected_snapshot_sha256": "<lineage-review snapshot SHA256>",
  "connection": "<configured collector alias>",
  "expected_workspace_id": "<actual collector workspace UUID>",
  "title": "Workbook lineage",
  "note": "Reviewed original import, complete query export and workbook.",
  "include_sql": false
}
~~~

The original service rechecks the reviewed snapshot, freezes the exact event bytes and binds the selected collector. A title is nonblank and at most 160 characters. Notes can be empty, at most 4000 characters, with ordinary tabs/newlines.

The result preserves the complete normalized `request`, the plan ID and SHA, source event SHA/length/name/URL, target binding and actual publication state. To recover an uncertain save, read `lineage-plan` using the same `plan_id` or repeat the exact original save request. Do not create another plan solely because the reply was lost.

`lineage-plans` lists compact summaries. Its `request_summary` is explicitly incomplete; retrieve `lineage-plan` for the full original replay request. Plan reads accept the same optional metadata collection paging.

## Publish and reopen the original job

Publish with:

~~~json
{
  "id": "<saved original publication job ID:32hex>",
  "plan_id": "<saved plan ID:32hex>",
  "plan_sha256": "<exact plan SHA256>"
}
~~~

Use operation `lineage-publish`. The helper reads the current original plan. If it already names a publication job, that job ID must match; the helper reads the actual original job before an explicit continuation. A completed job returns its retained result. Otherwise the original Analysis start/resume rules decide whether that same request can proceed.

After an uncertain reply, use `lineage-publication` with the same `id`. Its result is the actual original Analysis job, request, result, error and progress. An accepted result contains the original native collector receipt; completion is not inferred from a transport connection or a successful local command.

If work is still unwanted, `lineage-cancel` with that `id` requests cancellation of the original local worker. This returns the native progress envelope with `job_id`, `state`, `cancel_requested` and observations. Read `lineage-publication` afterward to see the actual job outcome. A complete accepted collector receipt remains accepted.

A saved plan can have an unknown dispatch outcome. Reuse its exact source, original job ID and collector key through the original continuation path. No helper operation creates a replacement key, changes the collector destination or automatically resends an uncertain publication.

## Select and read the exact delivery files

`lineage-downloads` accepts `{plan_id}` and returns the unchanged original native index:

~~~text
schema, workspace_id, plan_id, plan_sha256, events_sha256,
manifest_sha256, files[{name,bytes,sha256,mime}], index_sha256
~~~

The index has exactly these seven complete files:

| File | Original content |
|---|---|
| `events.json` | Exact event-source bytes submitted by this plan |
| `plan.json` | Original saved plan and selected publication view |
| `native-bindings.json` | Complete Analysis source and dependency bindings |
| `receipts.json` | Original publication observations and receipts |
| `report.html` | Human-readable original publication report |
| `manifest.json` | Full handover member identities |
| `handover.zip` | Complete portable delivery verified by the original reader |

The index hash is the original sorted-key UTF-8 canonical JSON digest. Its selected bytes may change when later publication observations are added. Preserve the exact returned `plan_sha256`, `index_sha256`, file SHA and byte count for a download.

`lineage-file` requires `{plan_id, plan_sha256, index_sha256, filename, sha256}` and optional `byteOffset` / `maxBytes`. The maximum chunk is 65536 bytes; the default is 32768. The first file read checks the current native index, receives the complete selected file (at most 128 MiB), verifies its exact size/hash and privately publishes it through the existing initialization helpers. Each subsequent range uses the existing SavedFileReader and its stable descriptor/hash check.

The result is:

~~~text
{
  planId, workspaceId, planSha256, indexSha256, filename,
  file: {bytes,sha256,contentType,byteOffset,returnedBytes,
         encoding:"base64",data,nextByteOffset,verifiedSavedFile:true}
}
~~~

Follow `file.nextByteOffset` until it is null. A cached original file remains tied to its original index even after a newer publication history changes the live index. If that old file was never saved and the current native index differs, the operation refuses the mismatch; inspect and review the new index rather than mixing editions.

The agent never supplies a cache path. The original host owns the private `analysis/lineage-files/<workspace>/<plan>/<index>/` directory beneath its registered native workspace. Local publication and file reads remain inside the parent's complete request/close lifetime.

## Download, resume and reopen with the CLI

The maintained entry point is `stellar-forge/mcp-paid-agent/native-analysis-lineage-download.mjs`. It uses the existing retained-download transport and saves all seven original members plus `lineage-download-index.json`.

~~~bash
node stellar-forge/mcp-paid-agent/native-analysis-lineage-download.mjs inspect \
  --url "$MCP_URL" --workspace analysis --plan "$PLAN_ID" --token-env MCP_TOKEN

node stellar-forge/mcp-paid-agent/native-analysis-lineage-download.mjs download \
  --url "$MCP_URL" --workspace analysis --plan "$PLAN_ID" --token-env MCP_TOKEN \
  --dir /absolute/private/lineage-delivery \
  --plan-sha256 "$PLAN_SHA256" --index-sha256 "$INDEX_SHA256" --chunk-size 32768

node stellar-forge/mcp-paid-agent/native-analysis-lineage-download.mjs reopen \
  --plan "$PLAN_ID" --dir /absolute/private/lineage-delivery \
  --plan-sha256 "$PLAN_SHA256" --index-sha256 "$INDEX_SHA256"
~~~

`--token-env` selects an existing environment variable when this MCP host requires it; omit it for a host configured without that credential. Tokens are not command-line values.

Repeat `download` with the same directory and identities after a lost range reply or MCP restart. The original download checkpoint binds its exact verified prefix and exclusive final publication. `reopen` verifies the complete saved files and index without a live host or collector.

The original Python handover reader can then inspect the complete exported archive offline:

~~~python
from stellar_forge_buyer.analysis_lineage_reports import LineagePublication

publication = LineagePublication(
    "/absolute/private/lineage-delivery/handover.zip",
    expected_sha256="<exact handover.zip SHA256 from the saved index>",
)
review = publication.inspect()
print(review["plan_id"], review["events_sha256"])
print(review["summary"])
~~~

The constructor verifies all original handover members, plan/event digests and accepted native receipt. `publication.plan`, `.snapshot`, `.receipts`, `.events` and `.manifest` are the retained parsed values. `publication.native_document(sha256)` returns a selected exact verified original document. This reader has no context-manager or close method and makes no collector call.

## Receiving and deployment

Ship these additive helper/schema/guide leaves with the original Analysis dispatcher, schema imports, native file reader and complete original initialization module. The dispatcher owns HTTP capability/origin checks, response bounds, cancellation and draining through local publication.

The existing full receiving programme reuses one saved plan and its accepted publication ID. It reads the original plan and job, repeats the exact saved request, downloads the native files, interrupts a real retained prefix, reopens the same MCP workspace at a new port, resumes into the same directory and verifies the delivery offline. It creates no second Analysis run or collector publication.

Source publication, syntax/import checks and an executed native receiving result are separate evidence. The operating commands above do not claim that a receiving run has completed.

## Complete dataset-to-report workflow

### Attach the actual completed delivery

Use the original native dataset history/status/delivery actions to select the exact acquisition. Finish its original delivery before attaching it. This analytical operation never creates missing pages.

~~~json
{
  "action": "analysis",
  "analysisWorkspace": "customer",
  "analysisOperation": "attach-dataset",
  "analysisRequest": {
    "acquisition_id": "the-retained-native-acquisition-id",
    "name": "received_inventory",
    "expected_revision": 0
  }
}
~~~

Revision zero creates an unused source alias. Read sources and pass the actual current revision when intentionally replacing one.

The host resolves the acquisition ID through the original completedDataset method, which verifies its COMPLETE session, configuration, source binding and finalized SF100 files. Immediately before the original source-registration transaction, the Python adapter reopens that same existing room through SF88/SF100, requires zero appended pages, and checks unchanged original session/manifest identities. The source record retains native_delivery provenance.

### Import and select the reviewed edition

Start import with a stable 32-character lowercase hexadecimal ID and the exact returned source revision:

~~~json
{
  "action": "analysis",
  "analysisWorkspace": "customer",
  "analysisOperation": "import",
  "analysisRequest": {
    "id": "10000000000000000000000000000001",
    "source": "received_inventory",
    "source_revision": 1
  }
}
~~~

Example IDs here are placeholders: generate a new ID for a new operation and retain it for recovery. Use job with that same ID until the original status is terminal. COMPLETE returns its immutable version_id, original source identity, table and columns. Optional columns_text is a JSON object mapping original fields to SQL column names through the existing importer.

Read version and manifest to review the original query filters, projection, ordering, snapshot and receipts. Activate the exact edition:

~~~json
{
  "action": "analysis",
  "analysisWorkspace": "customer",
  "analysisOperation": "activate",
  "analysisRequest": {
    "name": "inventory",
    "version_id": "EXACT_64_CHARACTER_VERSION_ID_FROM_IMPORT",
    "expected_revision": 0
  }
}
~~~

Use the actual current revision for an existing view. The original compare-and-swap preserves history and rejects stale selections.

For a changed edition, compare accepts the reviewed view/revision, base_version_id, candidate_version_id and explicit unique non-null typed keys. Comparison pages retain source scope, schema/value changes and row positions. Select records the exact comparison review and atomically selects its candidate through the original view CAS.

Changing a five-row inventory query to a three-row widget filter does not establish that two upstream stock records were deleted. Keep the different query/projection scope in the review note; original source facts and decisions flow into the report.

### Save SQL and export its complete output

For the merchant inventory example:

~~~json
{
  "action": "analysis",
  "analysisWorkspace": "customer",
  "analysisOperation": "save-query",
  "analysisRequest": {
    "name": "inventory_by_availability",
    "expected_revision": 0,
    "sql": "SELECT available, COUNT(*) AS records, SUM(units) AS units FROM inventory GROUP BY available ORDER BY available",
    "parameters_text": "[]",
    "max_rows": 1000
  }
}
~~~

Read state after reviewing the selected data. Copy its entire original views array into a query request's expected_views, along with the actual SQL, parameters_text, max_rows and stable job ID. The original read-only SQL transaction rejects a changed selection. Job pages retain typed values and the explicit truncated flag.

Use parameters_text JSON to preserve signed 64-bit integers and fixed-decimal strings. SQL cells retain original typed-text encoding. Raw unsafe integers in source metadata use {"encoding":"json-integer","text":"..."} in the MCP response; original stored bytes and hashes remain unchanged.

For a complete extract, call query-export with the COMPLETE query ID and its original result_sha256:

~~~json
{
  "action": "analysis",
  "analysisWorkspace": "customer",
  "analysisOperation": "query-export",
  "analysisRequest": {
    "id": "10000000000000000000000000000002",
    "query_id": "EXACT_32_CHARACTER_COMPLETED_QUERY_ID",
    "result_sha256": "EXACT_64_CHARACTER_QUERY_RESULT_SHA256",
    "label": "Reviewed inventory extract",
    "formats": ["jsonl", "csv", "sqlite"],
    "timeout": 300,
    "spreadsheet_safe": true
  }
}
~~~

The original controller binds the saved SQL, exact parameters and reviewed views, then streams complete outputs. Optional positive max_rows and max_output_bytes are explicit ceilings; reaching a ceiling is not a complete export.

Use job or query-exports for progress and cancel-query-export for original worker cancellation. A published complete native manifest remains complete after a late cancellation or interruption.

After COMPLETE, query-export-file reads the job's selected manifest.json, rows.jsonl, rows.csv or rows.sqlite3. It checks the original job/request/source identity and native manifest, selects `analysis-query-exports/JOB_ID` under the host-registered customer database, and reuses the shared verified saved-file descriptor/hash cache. A copied workspace keeps the earlier producer directory in its original result; that provenance never selects a file path. Unchanged file ranges do not rerun SQL, copy the output or hash/download its entire payload again. Preserve the returned SHA256 across ranges.

### Retain and publish a complete report

A saved report pins 1–12 original query revisions:

~~~json
{
  "action": "analysis",
  "analysisWorkspace": "customer",
  "analysisOperation": "save-report",
  "analysisRequest": {
    "name": "inventory_review",
    "id": "10000000000000000000000000000003",
    "expected_revision": 0,
    "title": "Received inventory review",
    "introduction": "The selected source is the original delivered inventory query described in its retained manifest.",
    "sections": [
      {

        "query_revision": 1

~~~

Sections can override exact parameters_text. Start report using a stable ID and the returned name, revision, definition_sha256 and full reviewed expected_views. The original engine reads all sections in one SQLite snapshot, retains source editions/data-review decisions, and commits completed rows and result identity together. Section truncation remains explicit.

Use report-read to review each section and its original result hash/publication_revision. Publish accepts report_id, a new stable id, exact result_sha256, expected_revision and note. It freezes the retained completed report without rerunning queries. Publications returns the immutable records and their SHA256 values.

Start report-export with the chosen publication_id, publication_sha256, new job id and html/json/csv format. CSV uses the original multi-section ZIP with metadata and section files. Read the COMPLETE result through file. Reports, comparison exports and backups use the same original saved-file reader.

Every file response identifies the full file and returns at most 64 KiB of base64 bytes. Continue with nextByteOffset, preserving sha256 from the first reply.

## Operation and recovery behavior

| Situation | Continue through the original state |
| --- | --- |
| Connection lost while starting a job | Read job using the same ID. A lost reply does not require a replacement acquisition or analytical operation. |
| Job already COMPLETE | Read its original retained result/files. |
| Same report, selection or publication request repeated | Original ID/request hash returns the historical result; changed input under that ID is rejected. |
| Source/view revision changed | Read the current original selection, review it, then intentionally submit the new revision. |
| Save-query reply uncertain | Read saved-query and its revision first. This original API uses revision CAS, not a request ID. |
| Python service restarted | Start the same original database; the adapter reads its new launch record and checks workspace identity. |
| Native adapter closes | Its requests close; the host-owned analysis process keeps its original lifecycle. |
| Full export interrupted | The original controller adopts a complete native manifest without query replay; unfinished work stays explicitly failed/cancelled/interrupted. |

Dataset source aliases are current pointers. If an alias changed after an older import, reopen that original job ID for its historical outcome rather than reconstructing it from today's alias.

## Backup and reopen

Start backup with a stable ID and read its COMPLETE native SQLite file through file. It contains imported rows, exact source manifests, mappings, selected-view history, recipes, comparisons/decisions, reports and publications.

The original native session/page/evidence/SF100 files, raw response files, full-query export directories, generated report files and native MCP alias registrations remain outside the SQLite backup. Retain them separately for new source work or existing external file downloads.

Save the verified backup bytes as datasets.sqlite3 in a new private directory, then start the original AnalysisWorkspace there. Register a new native analytical alias for that running service. The restored database preserves its original analytical identity and histories.

Copied full-query exports and customer workbooks can reopen their existing bytes when their complete original `analysis-query-exports/JOB_ID` or `analysis-workbooks/BUILD_ID` directories are retained under the registered receiving database. The adapter derives local paths from that selected database and validated job ID, preserves the producer location in the original result, and checks the original manifest and file digests. Copied complete report/change exports and SQLite backups likewise resolve from the selected receiving database and their original job, filename and file-hash bindings. A database backup alone does not restore external export or workbook files.

The original database service remains the single process/worker owner. This integration needs no additional scheduler, proxy, lock service or recovery daemon.

### Review the saved original selection

These examples use the original host SDK dispatcher. The caller selects the
actual returned connection and dossier; the variable names below are not
new identifiers or provider credentials.

~~~js
const call = async (analysisOperation, analysisRequest = {}) =>
  (await native.call({
    action: 'analysis',
    analysisWorkspace: 'customer',
    analysisOperation,
    analysisRequest
  })).result;

const configured = await call('research-connections');
// Select the intended returned connection using its actual name.
const connection = configured.connections.find(
  item => item.name === selectedConnectionName
);
if (!connection) throw new Error('Select a configured Research connection.');
const base = {
  connection: connection.name,
  expected_workspace_id: connection.workspace_id
};

const first = await call('research-dossiers', {...base, limit: 20});
const nextCursor = first.result.next;
if (nextCursor) {
  const next = await call('research-dossiers', {...base, ...nextCursor});
  // next.result belongs to the same original inventory snapshot.
}
~~~

The native outer envelope has its own `result` field. The four
Research read operations then preserve the original intake wrapper:
`{connection, workspace_id, dossier_id?, family?, result}`.
The inventory is therefore `first.result` after the helper
above unwraps the native outer envelope. Preserve the entire original
inventory `next` object. A nonzero offset requires its exact
snapshot; a changed inventory is returned by the original service as a
reviewable error.

Read sources using the actual dossier ID and family:

~~~js
const picked = {
  ...base,
  dossier_id: selectedDossierId,
  family: selectedFamily
};
const listed = await call('research-sources', {...picked, limit: 20});
~~~

The original dossier ID is `d_<UUID>`, including its hyphens.
Use the original returned Documents or Pipelines cursor as
`after` for another saved-source page. Managed provider job,
file and node IDs remain the native values returned with that source.

Select exactly one of these source forms:

| Family | Original `selection` |
| --- | --- |
| Documents | `{purchaseId: 'u_<64 hex>'}` or `{editionId: 'e_<64 hex>'}` |
| Pipelines | `{operationId: 'up_<64 hex>', outputId: 'out_<64 hex>'}` or `{editionId: 'e_<64 hex>'}` |

Use actual returned IDs in place of the notation. A selection keeps its
native shape and family; it is never regenerated from row order.

~~~js
const selected = {...picked, selection: selectedOriginalSource};
const reviewed = await call('research-review', selected);
const editionSha256 = reviewed.result.editionSha256;

const page = await call('research-elements', {

  limit: 25,
  page: '',
  type: '',

});
~~~

The exact review digest is
`reviewed.result.editionSha256`. Element filtering changes the
displayed page. Capture retains the complete selected original edition and

### Recover the same original capture

A lost native tool reply leaves the exact original capture request as the
recovery unit. Read `job` using its retained ID first. If
accepted, that job contains the original request and actual status/result.
Explicitly repeating `research-capture` with every unchanged
request field resumes the existing original capture. A different selection,
digest, source revision or timestamp requires a new reviewed request.

The source-registration transaction is authoritative. If it completed before
the job result reply was retained, the original intake searches its registered
source closure first and completes that same capture. A matching restored
source can finish this recovery with the Research connection unavailable.

`research-captures` pages original history by its returned
`next_before` sequence. It keeps compact document/digest/
verification results; `job` opens the complete selected
receipt and mapping.

~~~js
await call('research-cancel', {id: exactCapture.id});
const observed = await call('job', {id: exactCapture.id});
~~~

Cancellation belongs to the existing local capture worker and its original
Research-client calls. A completed source registration remains available and
complete. Closing the native MCP adapter drains its own requests through the
existing Analysis lifetime; the host's service and saved jobs retain their
normal ownership.

For a portable delivery, use the original whole-workspace archive. It includes
the registered original source documents, exact mapping and imported data,
capture history, selected original query/workbook outputs and their
manifests. The restored Analysis service can reopen those local documents
under a newly registered native workspace alias.

## Reviewed lineage and portable handover

Use the [Analysis lineage agent workflow](ANALYSIS_LINEAGE.md) to discover operator-selected collector connections, review dependencies from completed native jobs, save an exact publication plan, publish or reopen its original job, and receive the complete hash-bound handover. The same original Analysis workspace owns its browser, Python and MCP history. The installed `mcp-analysis-lineage-download` command uses the maintained retained-file transfer and supports same-directory continuation and offline complete reopen. It does not execute the original query or acquire data again.

# Frictionless Data Package merchant

Turn a retained [Frictionless Data Package](https://datapackage.org/standard/data-package/) into a reviewed, versioned dataset served by the existing Starforge merchant. The package reader retains the publisher's exact descriptor, CSV/TSV/JSON/Parquet data, external schemas and dialects, source references and licensing metadata. The original SF30 publisher owns extraction, review, publication, schedules and its browser; the original SF82 store owns merchant releases; the original SF88/SF100 customer workflow owns acquired pages.

## Run the product

Requires Linux, Python 3.10+, Node 22.16+ and util-linux `flock`. CSV, TSV and JSON use Python's standard library. Parquet uses the already maintained Wherobots PyArrow decoder and its optional installed runtime, described below. Set `SF_FRICTIONLESS_PYTHON` to a trusted installed Python executable when `python3` is not the selected runtime.

From the repository root:

~~~bash
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/frictionless/cli.mjs --help
~~~

The maintained distribution exposes `starforge frictionless`. The original dataset command also accepts `node dataset-cli.mjs frictionless ...`. The examples below use the direct CLI from the `frictionless` directory.

Use canonical private directories and owner-only source/configuration files. The original publisher takes a writer lease: close its browser server before opening that same workspace through another CLI process.

## 1. Capture an original package edition

~~~bash
node cli.mjs capture --descriptor /private/source/datapackage.json --output /private/package-20261012
node cli.mjs inspect-capture --capture /private/package-20261012/capture.json
node cli.mjs suggest-source --capture /private/package-20261012/capture.json --output /private/package-source.json
~~~

The descriptor may be a local path or HTTPS URL. Local relative resource references resolve from the original descriptor; HTTPS references remain HTTPS through redirects. A package may contain multiple named tabular resources, multiple paths for one resource, or inline data. `--resource NAME` selects named resources; omit it to capture the whole package. Repeat `--reference PATH_OR_HTTPS_URL` to retain original documentation needed for a schema review.

A capture has a create-only directory, complete manifest and content-addressed original files. Each file is bound to its byte length and SHA-256, with original retrieval URL, redirect destination and available HTTP metadata. Descriptor, schema and dialect references remain attached to their original resource. Package and resource licensing metadata stays in inspection and in the release's retained source.

Inspection reads the complete selected tables and reports per-resource row counts, field metadata, declared missing markers, empty cells, keys and errors. A resource requiring review does not prevent the report from describing other resources.

## 2. Review the projection and source semantics

The suggested configuration preserves physical strings and literal missing markers. Review this source before creating the publication plan:

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.frictionless-source.v1",
  "connection": {
    "file": "/private/package-20261012/capture.json",
    "sha256": "THE_CAPTURE_SHA256_RETURNED_BY_CAPTURE"
  },
  "queries": {
    "monthly": {
      "resource": "co2-mm-mlo",
      "projection": {
        "Month": {
          "field": "Date",
          "type": "string",
          "missing": "literal",
          "representation": "physical"
        },
        "Average": {
          "field": "Average",
          "type": "string",
          "missing": "literal",
          "representation": "physical"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
~~~

Use each resource's inspected field names. The example shows the configuration shape; the original NOAA monthly package described below needs its reviewed full schema before publication.

Each output alias must be a safe native dataset column name. Each projection explicitly chooses a source field, native type, representation and missing-value policy:

| Choice | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `type: string`, `representation: physical` | Preserves source scalar text for text formats; Parquet uses the exact typed representation described below. |
| `type: integer` | Requires a logical integer exactly representable by the native JavaScript integer range. |
| `type: number` | Requires a finite logical number whose decimal value survives the native JSON number representation exactly. |
| `type: boolean` | Uses the source schema's accepted boolean representation. |
| `missing: literal` | Preserves the original marker as text; use a string projection. |
| `missing: null` | Produces native null and marks the dataset column nullable. |
| `missing: reject` | Stops extraction when a declared missing value occurs. |

Field-level `missingValues` overrides the schema list. An absent list uses the standard empty-string marker. An empty string cannot simultaneously mean an actual string and null in the same native CSV column; choose a projection that keeps those meanings distinct.

Logical numbers use decimal parsing before conversion. Values outside the native integer range, extra decimal precision, numeric underflow and a changed negative-zero representation produce a useful projection error; preserving physical text keeps the original value available. Date, datetime, time, year and year-month metadata remain attached to their source fields. Original month strings remain month strings.

The reader supports the relevant [Table Schema](https://datapackage.org/standard/table-schema/) scalar types, required/unique/primary keys, supported field constraints, explicit field lists, and [Table Dialect](https://datapackage.org/standard/table-dialect/) CSV settings. Keys are checked over the complete selected resource using a private SQLite index. CSV parsing includes quoted/multiline values, declared encoding, delimiter/quote/escape settings, header rows and joins, comments and explicit no-header tables. Quoted values beginning with a comment character remain data.

Foreign keys, custom profiles, JSON Schema constraints and domain-specific structures such as GeoJSON retain their original definitions and review notes. Apply the source's additional domain checks when selecting those fields. The inspection result describes the reader's supported checks.

### Resolve stale source metadata explicitly

A query may include a reviewed `schemaOverride`, `schemaReview` and supported `dialect` overrides. The schema review must record a reason and exact original references already captured with `--reference`:

~~~json
{
  "schemaOverride": {
    "fields": [
      {"name": "Month", "type": "yearmonth"},
      {"name": "DecimalDate", "type": "number"},
      {"name": "Average", "type": "number"},
      {"name": "Deseasonalized", "type": "number"},
      {"name": "NumberOfDays", "type": "integer"},
      {"name": "StandardDeviation", "type": "number"},
      {"name": "Uncertainty", "type": "number"}
    ],
    "primaryKey": ["Month"]
  },
  "schemaReview": {
    "reason": "The package's monthly CSV has seven fields; its older header and schema have six. Use NOAA's retained current column definitions, accounting for the package's combined year-month field.",
    "sources": ["https://gml.noaa.gov/webdata/ccgg/trends/co2/co2_mm_mlo.csv"]
  },
  "dialect": {"header": false, "commentRows": [1]}
}
~~~

Place these properties inside the selected query, alongside `resource` and `projection`; the projection then names the reviewed fields. The complete original descriptor, original header and supporting NOAA file remain retained. An intentionally excluded blank record can be named in `commentRows`; blank rows are otherwise read.

~~~bash

node cli.mjs plan --source /private/package-source.json --query monthly --out /private/monthly-plan.json
~~~

The plan carries the selected exact types and nullability into the original CSV schema. Review its exposed columns, enabled filters/ranges/sorts, complete extraction order and resource limits. Ordering has an explicit original-member/record tie breaker and nulls last. Exceeding row, byte, row-size or time limits stops the extraction; the published candidate must be complete.

~~~bash
python3 - /private/original-reviewed-plan.json /private/received-plan.json <<'PY'

import sys
from pathlib import Path

original = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())
destination = Path(sys.argv[2])

    raise SystemExit("Choose the original reviewed named query.")
dataset_fields = (
    "name", "columns", "filters", "ranges", "sorts",
    "maxCellChars", "defaultLimit", "maxLimit", "maxPageBytes",
)
received.update(
    title=original["title"],
    query=original["query"],

             if key in original["dataset"]},
    extraction=original["extraction"],
)
destination.write_text(json.dumps(received, indent=2) + "\n")
PY
~~~

The same capture, source review, publication, merchant release and source-transfer commands accept a resource with `format: parquet`. ### Use the original installed Arrow runtime

The Parquet adapter imports the maintained [Wherobots output reader](../wherobots/source/wherobots_operator/editions.py). The adapter applies the existing Frictionless field mapping, schema checks and reviewed projection.

Use the trusted Python interpreter already configured with the Wherobots PyArrow requirement. The current original [requirements](../wherobots/source/requirements.txt) pin `pyarrow==26.0.0`. "$SF_FRICTIONLESS_PYTHON" -c 'import pyarrow; print(pyarrow.__version__)'
~~~bash
node cli.mjs inspect-capture --capture /private/pudl-release/capture.json
~~~

Inspection records the actual installed PyArrow version, physical column types and nullability, complete metadata row count, row-group count, original geometry metadata when present, and each member's exact byte length and SHA-256. The original reader processes bounded batches with its threaded/prebuffered reads disabled. The normal private-file checks and a before/after file identity check cover the retained source while the native reader is open.

### Review typed values before publication

A Parquet file contains typed values rather than an original CSV spelling. Its complete binary bytes remain in the source capture. The physical string projection uses these representations:

| Original Parquet value | Retained projection representation |
| --- | --- |
| Null | Native null when the projection chooses `missing: null`; choose a missing policy explicitly. |
| String and dictionary string | The complete original string, including leading zeroes. |
| Signed or unsigned integer | Decimal integer text, without conversion through a floating-point value. |
| Decimal | Decimal text with the original value and scale represented by Arrow's Decimal value. |
| Finite floating-point number | Python's round-tripping representation of the original native value. The original binary file retains its bit representation. |
| Boolean | `true` or `false`. |
| Date | ISO calendar date. |
| Timestamp | Exact epoch ticks rendered as ISO datetime, keeping the original seconds/milliseconds/microseconds/nanoseconds and declared timezone. |
| Time | Exact clock time at the original unit precision. |
| Duration | Exact signed ISO seconds duration. |
| Binary, list, map or struct | The existing reader's lossless JSON representation, including its original typed markers. |

Logical schema validation still precedes projection. A native numeric publication requires an exact finite value; a reviewed physical string projection can retain declared NaN or infinity when the source constraints allow it. A typed structure that does not meet its declared scalar schema requires a source review. Schema constraints and required/unique/primary-key checks run over the complete resource. The native dataset's safe integer and number rules remain unchanged; a string representation retains larger integers and decimals when a native numeric column cannot represent them exactly.

A resource's Table Schema matches columns by the existing `fieldsMatch` contract, including exact, equal, subset, superset and partial matches. Physical column names and schema field names stay bound through that mapping. CSV dialect overrides are rejected for Parquet. The original descriptor and its declared dialect remain retained for source review.

The reader checks the declared required/unique/primary keys. It retains all foreign-key declarations for the selected resources. The migration operator separately checks the concrete joins that the selected customer workflow uses:
