stellar-forge frictionless-agent serve --config MERCHANT.json --workspace ALIAS --port 0 --mcp-port 0
stellar-forge frictionless-source --help
~~~

The existing **stellar-forge frictionless workbench** command exposes the same source client. Full host configuration, browser steps and agent tools are documented in [FRICTIONLESS_WORKSPACE.md](../../../../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/FRICTIONLESS_WORKSPACE.md). Complete delivered-source instructions are in [RECEIVING.md](RECEIVING.md).

Configure a workspace alias against an already declared publisher of kind **frictionless**. Its inputs are host-declared descriptor files, public HTTPS descriptors or complete original source archives. The built-in **current** alias points to the publisher's presently selected source. A client selects aliases; it does not supply arbitrary filesystem paths or new credential destinations.

## Complete operator workflow

The browser opens the source panel above the existing publisher controls.

| Screen | Operator outcome |
|---|---|
| Source inputs | Inspect the declared input identity and explicitly retain one complete native capture. |
| Resources | Read original schemas, field inspection, rights/references and every captured file. |
| Source editions | Author ordered projections or edit exact query JSON; retain each revision as an immutable edition. |
| Review and select | Run the original full native review, read its findings and select a reviewed edition with the current publisher source hash. |
| Publication plan | Obtain the native query's original plan template, save it with a stable request identity and open that exact plan in the existing publisher. |
| Compare captures | Read the original descriptor, schema, dialect and file-hash comparison between two retained source captures. |
| Source receiving | Export the source archive and all selected-edition commissioning records, then receive every declared file. |
| Requests | Inspect actual native outcomes, open saved inputs/results and explicitly resume or cancel the original request. |

Intake retains a capture even when a suggested query still needs correction. Source edition creation and full review use the existing native validators. A completed review operation and a successful source review are separate states; publication requires an applicable successful review.

The query editor accepts **queriesText**, an exact JSON string. Original source inspection provides this string from Python serialization. Large integer constraints and column insertion order therefore survive browser/client reopen. Structured **queries** remains supported for safely representable input. Native numeric and missing-value semantics remain with the original parser.

## Publisher source selection and original plans

The maintained publisher now supports source selection only for its opting-in Frictionless driver. Selection runs under the original writer and checks the current source hash and the selected immutable source bytes. The original configured source remains in the workspace metadata as its initial binding; the latest retained source selection supplies subsequent operations.

Before the first selection, the workspace marker advances to the Frictionless-compatible v2 form. A runtime that only understands the original v1 marker cannot silently continue using the initial source. The maintained Frictionless driver, merchant configuration reader and release path all recognize the new marker.

Source selection and its original event commit together. Publication-plan saving optionally receives a caller-retained request UUID; the plan, its request binding and original event commit in the same transaction. A repeated exact request resolves the original saved plan, including after a lost response. Previously saved plans retain their own source capture and can still be inspected.

Opening a saved plan in the browser delegates to the original publisher host. The original dirty-plan confirmation, native validation and extraction/review/publication flow remain in force.

## Requests, files and ownership

The private workbench directory is inside the original publisher workspace. It uses the maintained Linux writer lease and a full-sync SQLite journal. Each mutation retains its UUID, exact ordered input and applicable version before work begins. Startup marks an ended active request interrupted; it does not launch it.

Native operations use the original source process runner. Closing the workbench cancels and drains only its own active source task. The merchant borrowing lease owns the workbench model, retained readers and borrowed browser, and releases them before the original publisher owner closes.

The source browser is an original loopback, origin-checked publisher listener. MCP authentication stays with the original merchant server. Browser capability/instance details are not embedded into portable source files.

Complete native inspection, review and comparison reports are retained as the original Python response bytes. Browser summaries are views; their corresponding file downloads preserve the full original JSON. Export snapshots freeze the original edition, capture inspection, all then-retained reviews, source-selection history, saved-plan bindings and receiving guide before native source export begins.

The agent file and download interfaces reuse the original retained-file reader and resumable downloader. A descriptor binds workspace/export identity, original manifest, each file's full digest and its byte offset. Original reader release and owner reopening are handled by that same client.

## Native model and browser integration

The model entry point is **openFrictionlessSourceWorkbench({publisher, inputs, environment})**. It receives an already owned original Frictionless publisher. Its methods expose status/current/input/capture/edition/review/planInput/comparison/operation, explicit start/resume/cancel/wait and exact retained files.

The server entry point is **startFrictionlessSourceServer({workspace, port, ownsWorkspace, schedule})**. A borrowed listener requires the owner's original scheduler and closes only its listener. The merchant adapter borrows through the existing MerchantPublisher lifecycle; it does not open a parallel publisher.

The source-owned distribution contribution includes the command aliases, client exports, merchant provider, Applications provider, complete browser assets and receiving guide. The original Frictionless distribution supplies its maintained parser and optional Parquet decoder closure.

## Receiving and validation scope

Use [RECEIVING.md](RECEIVING.md) to download and reopen the full source handover. Use the original dataset/SF100 and customer workflows when a delivery also includes published data, customer reports or a warehouse.

This source change does not record a new provider purchase or customer acceptance. Native operating results belong to their explicit original operation records. The original NOAA customer operation remains a separate retained run using its already captured public input.

# Receive and reopen a Frictionless source edition

This directory carries one immutable source edition and its original commissioning records. Start with **manifest.json** and **source-edition.json**, then receive **source.tar.gz** through the original Frictionless source receiver.

The original package descriptor, resource files, captured reference files, schemas, dialect and source rights travel inside the native source archive. The workbench also retains the exact query JSON text, complete native reviews, original source selections and saved publication-plan bindings for the exported edition. Publication and customer processing continue through their existing dataset and customer handovers.

## Files and identities

| File | Meaning |
|---|---|
| manifest.json | Original workbench export UUID, workspace UUID, edition UUID, original source/capture hashes and every delivered member's byte count and SHA-256. |
| source.tar.gz | Complete native source archive made by the original Frictionless exporter. Its internal manifest binds the original source configuration and every captured file. |
| source-edition.json | Frozen edition/capture metadata, exact queriesText, the selected review, all then-retained source selections and saved-plan bindings for this edition. |
| capture-inspection.json | The original full native capture inspection, or an explicitly marked original inspection-error record when intake retained a source that still needed a query correction. |
| reviews/UUID.json | Every native review for this edition retained when export began, with each original report preserved as exact bytes. |
| RECEIVING.md | These receiving and reopening instructions, declared in the original export manifest. |
| Frictionless-Source-Download.json | Additional complete download descriptor written by the merchant client. It binds the native manifest and all of its files to the original workspace and export UUID. |

The native export manifest lists its content files; the merchant download descriptor additionally binds **manifest.json** itself. The download client may retain its own checkpoint files beside these members. Those files belong to the transfer operation and should remain when continuing an interrupted transfer.

Read source rights and references from the original descriptor and captured material. An export preserves those declarations; it does not grant additional data rights or independently establish scientific validity.

## Obtain every declared file

Use the installed merchant source client against the original MCP URL returned by the source-workbench launcher. Supply the token through the already selected host environment variable; keep its value outside commands and reports.

~~~sh
stellar-forge frictionless-source download \
  --url ORIGINAL_MCP_URL \
  --workspace ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE_ALIAS \
  --workspace-id ORIGINAL_WORKBENCH_UUID \
  --id ORIGINAL_EXPORT_UUID \
  --directory /private/received-source-handover \
  --token-env MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN
~~~

Use the exact original workspace and export IDs from the completed export operation. The receiver reads the original complete manifest before downloading its members. It retains offsets, verifies already received prefixes and confirms each full file's length and SHA-256 before committing the completed transfer.

If the connection closes, run the **same command with the same receiving directory and IDs**. The existing receiver reopens released file readers with their original digest and byte offset. A completed file is reused after verification. Reconnection does not start another source capture, review or export.

When the merchant process has reopened, first reopen the same declared workbench through **merchant_frictionless_open**, then inspect its persistent workspace UUID. The new instance IDs describe the new owner lifetime; the workbench UUID and existing export UUID remain the receiving identity. Use the listener that belongs to that reopened owner. Changing a transfer's endpoint or immutable binding requires its explicit original receiver recovery rules, rather than editing checkpoint files.

The browser's **Source receiving** view offers the native manifest and each exact file. For a full handover with many review files, the client command above receives every declared member and retains the complete transfer state. Keep all declared members together.

## Receive the original source archive

Use the same installed source distribution that contains the Frictionless source exporter and receiver. The source commands use Node, the original Python parser and its supported dependencies. Set **SF_FRICTIONLESS_PYTHON** to the configured Python executable when it differs from the host default. CSV, TSV and JSON use the original standard-library parser. Parquet uses the original selected decoder and its declared Python requirements.

Read the **source.tar.gz** SHA-256 from the verified export manifest. Select a new private output directory:

~~~sh
stellar-forge frictionless source-receive \
  --archive /private/received-source-handover/source.tar.gz \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --output /private/received-native-source
~~~

The original receiver checks the complete archive, validates its members and writes the received source atomically. Keep its actual return value with the source handover. The resulting **source.json** refers to the received capture. **original-source.json** retains the exact exporting source configuration.

The source configuration's hash may change when its capture path is relocated. The exported **source-edition.json** separately records:

- **edition.sourceHash**, the original immutable exporting source configuration.
- **capture.captureSha256**, the original capture manifest identity.
- **queriesText**, the exact original query definitions.
- **receivingSourceHash**, the source identity from the exporter's verified receiving copy.

Use the original receiver's actual source path and fresh inspection when working in another directory. Compare the capture identity, original source bytes and query definitions; do not replace a current source hash with an old path-dependent hash.

Once reception completes, reopening reads the existing **source.json**. Keep the received directory intact. Do not use another source-receive invocation to overwrite it.

## Review the received source

Run the original full source review against the received source configuration:

~~~sh
stellar-forge frictionless review-source \
  --source /private/received-native-source/source.json
~~~

The native review reads every selected row and applies the declared field, key, missing-value, type, schema and dialect contract. Preserve its actual result alongside the originating reviews. A source operation can complete with validation findings; inspect its reported resource states and issues before selecting that source for publication.

Original reports retain the previous environment's actual observation and reviewer. A receiving review is a new observation in the receiving environment. Preserve both, including corrections and unsuccessful reviews.

The workbench's exact **queriesText** is the portable query-editing input. Keep projected columns in their original order and preserve literal missing values. JSON integer constraints outside the exact JavaScript range should stay in this text form. The original Python handling of decimal JSON numbers remains unchanged; represent precision-sensitive text according to the source's native contract instead of silently narrowing it through a browser number.

## Reopen in the source workbench

Add the exported archive to the receiving merchant's existing source-workbench connection under a host-selected alias:

~~~json
{
  "kind": "source-archive",
  "label": "Received source edition",
  "path": "/private/received-source-handover/source.tar.gz"
}
~~~

Keep the original connection schema and publisher alias. The installed **Frictionless source workbench** application opens the same configured publisher and scheduler under one merchant MCP owner.

1. Open the declared workbench and inspect its persistent workspace UUID.
2. Inspect this archive alias and retain the actual SHA-256 returned by the host.
3. Start one explicit intake using that SHA, the current workbench version and a caller-retained request UUID.
4. Read the retained capture's resources and original file list.
5. Create a receiving edition from **queriesText** in the original exported **source-edition.json**. A receiving edition has its own UUID while retaining the same original source meaning and capture.
6. Run the original full native review and retain its actual reviewer and result.
7. Inspect the publisher's current source hash, then select this reviewed edition using that exact current hash.
8. Obtain and review the original publication-plan template for the selected query. Save it through the original publisher, then continue its existing extraction, candidate review and publication controls.

The receiving workbench preserves its own edition and operation history. The exported original UUIDs remain source provenance; they are not rewritten to impersonate receiving operations.

## Recover a disconnected operation

The source workbench stores an original request before beginning its action. Browser requests retain their exact input before dispatch and store a confirmed native result before refreshing derived views.

For an uncertain result, use **Requests** or the native request client:

~~~sh
stellar-forge frictionless-source request \
  --url ORIGINAL_MCP_URL \
  --workspace ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE_ALIAS \
  --workspace-id ORIGINAL_WORKBENCH_UUID \
  --id ORIGINAL_REQUEST_UUID
~~~

If the retained action is incomplete and the original owner is available, explicitly resume that same request:

~~~sh
stellar-forge frictionless-source request \
  --url ORIGINAL_MCP_URL \
  --workspace ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE_ALIAS \
  --workspace-id ORIGINAL_WORKBENCH_UUID \
  --id ORIGINAL_REQUEST_UUID \
  --resume --wait
~~~

A browser reload reads retained state. It does not replay a mutation. A new UUID represents a new requested action; retain the original body, query order and UUID when recovering an interrupted operation.

A completed source export freezes the exact selected edition, reviews, source selections, saved-plan bindings and guide. Later reviews do not change an already started export. Reopening a completed export verifies and returns its original files.

## Operational scope and limits

This source handover carries a complete source archive and the selected edition's commissioning records. The publisher's full database, candidate rows, published dataset generations, payment records and customer warehouse are carried by their respective existing export workflows. Export those artifacts as well when the receiving work includes them.

The workbench permits up to 64 native queries per source edition. Its original native archive is limited to 256 MiB compressed and the source receiver applies its existing 512 MiB unpacked bound. The merchant receiver permits at most 10,000 declared files, including the native manifest, and 256 MiB per file; download and native manifest bounds are 64 MiB. Full row review remains subject to the original native source contract and its resource bounds.

Retain the complete handover, actual native return values, configuration selection and final source version used to receive it. Close borrowed browsers and file readers through their original owner. A browser close does not close the publisher or scheduler that another component still owns.

# OpenLineage in the merchant operator

The connected tools operate the same native HTTP workspace as the browser. Imports, event projections, saved editions, review history, results, and exports use the original workspace store and operation journal.

## Start the original workspace

Run the installed OpenLineage command, or the original source CLI:

~~~sh
node cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/path/to/lineage-project --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
~~~

The startup JSON and the project's private connection.json contain its workspaceId, instanceId, and local origin. For a token-protected server, add --token-file with a private plain-text token file.

## Select workspace and complete file aliases

Save an owned private JSON file with mode 0600. Paths are relative to that file unless absolute. The workspaceId must come from the original project's startup record. SHA-256 values must cover every byte of each original input file.

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.openlineage-workspace-host.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "operations": {
      "label": "Production lineage",
      "connectionFile": "./lineage-project/connection.json",
      "workspaceId": "REPLACE_WITH_ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE_UUID",
      "timeoutMs": 120000,
      "inputs": {
        "production-events": {
          "label": "Original production event export",
          "path": "./inputs/production-events.ndjson",
          "kind": "source",
          "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_COMPLETE_FILE_SHA256",
          "name": "production-events.ndjson",
          "sourceReference": "Original production OpenLineage export"
        },
        "quality-result": {
          "label": "Complete quality query result",
          "path": "./inputs/quality-result.csv",
          "kind": "result",
          "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_COMPLETE_FILE_SHA256",
          "name": "quality-result.csv",
          "mediaType": "text/csv",
          "sourceReference": "Original quality query and run reference"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
~~~

Add tokenFile to the workspace entry when required. Select the operator token for this merchant connection; a separate producer token applies only to native event intake. Its contents remain in the host; tool responses expose workspace identity and input metadata. A configuration supports 1–32 distinct workspace aliases and up to 128 complete input aliases per workspace.

The default host input capacity is 40 MiB. maxInputBytes may raise the host's file-reading capacity to 1 GiB, while the selected native route and original source ceiling still apply. The default native action request is 64 MiB including JSON/base64 overhead; source imports have a 256 MiB wire/decoded ceiling. Configure the receiving host and choose the matching capacity before transferring a larger complete source. A file beyond the configured capacity returns its original size error.

The selected application uses a literal HTTP loopback origin, 127.0.0.1 or ::1. Tool callers choose configured aliases, native entity keys, record collections, and retained object IDs.

## Install in the original merchant host

The source-owned contribution registers:

~~~json
{
  "merchantProviders": {
    "openlineage-workspaces": "stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openlineage-workspace/merchant-provider.mjs"
  }
}
~~~

An existing merchant-mcp.json selects the private connection file with:

~~~json
{
  "openlineageWorkspaceConnection": "/absolute/path/to/openlineage-host.json"
}
~~~

For a new merchant directory, call the provider's initialize hook or its native module:

~~~javascript
import { initializeLineageMerchantWorkspace } from "./mcp-setup.mjs";
const result = await initializeLineageMerchantWorkspace({
  directory: "/absolute/path/to/new-merchant",
  connection: "/absolute/path/to/openlineage-host.json",
  name: "Operations lineage"
});
console.log(result.configuration);
~~~

The optional provider declaration and initializer run inside the complete installed merchant distribution, where the original provider contract, release-store/configuration modules, and shared durability helpers are present. The initializer uses the original release-store initializer, private setup lock, immutable configuration publication, and full merchant configuration reader. Repeating the same setup recovers its existing release store and configuration.

## Core client without the full merchant distribution

The call/summary/close owner and host client use Node builtins plus this workspace's native client and pure tool catalog. They can be exercised beside the existing source application:

~~~javascript
import { readLineageWorkspaceConfiguration } from "./mcp-client.mjs";
import { MerchantOpenLineageWorkspaces } from "./mcp.mjs";
const host = await readLineageWorkspaceConfiguration("/absolute/path/to/openlineage-host.json");
const owner = new MerchantOpenLineageWorkspaces({ openlineageWorkspaces: host });
try {
  const selected = await owner.call("merchant_lineage_workspaces", {});
  const metadata = await owner.call("merchant_lineage_workspace_metadata", { workspace: "operations" });
  console.log(selected, metadata);
} finally {
  await owner.close();
}
~~~

Closing the borrowed owner aborts its local waits and drains its tasks. The native server remains available to its browser and other clients.

## Operator workflow

1. Call merchant_lineage_workspaces to choose the original workspace and inspect complete input aliases.
2. Call merchant_lineage_workspace_metadata and retain revision. Page merchant_lineage_records_read with collection, expectedRevision, offset, and limit. Follow nextOffset until null.
3. Verify an input with merchant_lineage_input. Import a complete source with merchant_lineage_import_file, supplying input, expectedSha256, operationId, and expectedRevision. Native merchant_lineage_source_import also accepts complete text or base64 within the host's tool request capacity.
For a compressed source, keep the original .gz input alias and its wire SHA-256, and pass contentEncoding: "gzip" to merchant_lineage_import_file or merchant_lineage_source_import. The saved request retains this encoding alongside the original bytes and operation identity. merchant_lineage_source_read with decode: true returns the original base64 plus verified decodedBase64 and decodedSha256; object ranges and source downloads remain the original compressed bytes. [PRODUCERS.md](PRODUCERS.md) also connects native producer HTTP clients to this same workspace.

4. Inspect original entities with merchant_lineage_entity_read. Read their complete events, facets, source attribution, and reviews. Use merchant_lineage_lineage_read for upstream/downstream nodes and edges at a chosen depth.
5. Save a named edition with merchant_lineage_edition_save. Compare it with another edition or the current workspace using merchant_lineage_edition_compare.
6. Save named review decisions with merchant_lineage_review_save, including title, reason, entityKeys, decision, and the optional editionId.
7. Attach a complete result with merchant_lineage_attach_file. Include its host-pinned input and SHA-256, entityKeys, editionId, sourceReference, operationId, and expectedRevision. Query or experiment details may accompany the attachment.
8. Call merchant_lineage_workspace_export with includeApplication true. Read all bytes of that retained export with merchant_lineage_export_read and its returned ID.
9. Receive and reopen the complete package through the original CLI:

~~~sh
node cli.mjs receive --input openlineage-workspace.json --out /absolute/path/to/received-project
node cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/path/to/received-project --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
~~~

The complete source export includes the original application and the retained event, source, edition, review, and result records.

## Complete records and original bytes

| Operation | Continuation |
| --- | --- |
| merchant_lineage_records_read | Keep collection, edition, and expectedRevision; continue at nextOffset until null. |
| merchant_lineage_object_read | Keep original id; concatenate each decoded base64 range in offset order until complete. |
| merchant_lineage_export_read | Keep export id; concatenate ranges in offset order until complete. |
| merchant_lineage_source_read | Returns the complete original object as base64 when it fits the tool response. |
| merchant_lineage_report_read | Returns complete JSON, CSV, or HTML report text. |

Range reads default to 262,144 bytes and accept 1–4,194,304 bytes. Verify the final reconstructed file's SHA-256 against its original id. Range bytes, offset, nextOffset, totalBytes, and completion state remain explicit.

Tool requests accept 128 KiB; host file aliases carry larger complete inputs. Complete responses accept 8 MiB. When an entity/report/record page exceeds that response capacity, use smaller native record pages or original object/export ranges. Oversized read responses return an explicit size error. A successfully saved mutation with an oversized response returns outcome CONFIRMED, its original operation ID and revision, and a complete export retrieval route. Its responseView.complete is false; the full saved response remains in the original operation journal and complete workspace package.

## Recovery and concurrency

Every mutation requires an operationId and expectedRevision. The native workspace stores successful operations with their input identity and replays a completed operation before checking its old revision.

After timeout, cancellation, connection interruption, or an unexpected server error, repeat the identical operation, including its original ID, expected revision, file SHA, and full input. The borrowed client's metadata records active operations and uncertain operation identities. The original workspace's operations collection is the durable server record; retaining the caller's exact request supports recovery across client restarts.

The client pins the workspace and application instance at attachment. A later server restart leaves that pin in place. Call merchant_lineage_connection to inspect the current host-selected instance, then merchant_lineage_reconnect with its exact expectedInstanceId. This explicitly connects to the same configured workspace. Recover the original mutation afterwards.

A revision conflict includes currentRevision. Read the changed workspace, review the intended edit against it, and submit the reviewed edit with a new operationId and current expectedRevision.

merchant_lineage_cancel cancels one active local wait by operationId. Its response identifies cancellation requested; the native server may already have saved that operation, so recover the original request.

## Errors and effects

Authentication, startup identity changes, source SHA changes, validation, revision conflicts, active writer responses, connection interruption, and uncertain mutations remain distinct. Provider errors carry their native HTTP status and details. Mutation recovery details include operation ID, expected revision, payload hash, configured workspace, and attached instance.

Read tools use the configured local workspace. Imports, saved editions, reviews, result attachments, and exports use the original native actions. Workspace exports write their retained complete package in the original project.

# Receive original pipeline events

Use the workspace's existing `POST /api/v1/lineage` endpoint for native OpenLineage HTTP producers. The same workspace receives the source, projects lineage, saves reviewed editions, and exports the complete application and original files.

The receiver accepts a JSON event, JSON event array, or JSON lines, either uncompressed or with `Content-Encoding: gzip`. It keeps the actual request body. For gzip, the source ID is the SHA-256 of the compressed wire bytes; the source record also retains the decoded byte count and SHA-256. Complete original downloads return those compressed bytes. Source inspection can display the verified decoded JSON.

## Start the selected workspace

Use the installed `starforge openlineage` command, or the received application's `node /absolute/application/cli.mjs` entry. The following examples use the native entry directly.

For an authenticated producer, select two different private token files. The operator token accesses the whole workspace. The producer token admits original events only at the native producer endpoint.

```sh
node /absolute/application/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /absolute/lineage-project \
  --port 8767 \
  --token-file /absolute/private/operator-token \
  --producer-token-file /absolute/private/producer-token
```

Both tokens must contain at least 24 characters, and they must differ. Keep the token files with the selected host's existing secret configuration. The application writes its nonsecret current connection to `/absolute/lineage-project/connection.json`.

The default listener is `127.0.0.1`. A pipeline running on that same host can use it directly. A remote deployment needs the operator's existing authenticated transport to this listener, retaining its expected Host and origin. The workspace does not deploy a proxy or alter network configuration.

A local unprotected workspace can omit both token flags. A workspace configured with only the operator token retains its existing common-token behavior.

## Generate private producer settings

Generate settings from the actual connection file, using the producer's token file:

```sh
node /absolute/application/cli.mjs producer-config \
  --connection /absolute/lineage-project/connection.json \
  --token-file /absolute/private/producer-token \
  --client python \
  --compression gzip \
  --timeout 30 \
  --out /absolute/private/python-openlineage.yaml
```

The command creates a new private file and prints its path, workspace identity and authentication status. It keeps the token out of standard output. The output is a complete JSON document, also valid YAML, containing the client's native `transport` configuration. Point the producer's existing OpenLineage configuration loader at that file using `OPENLINEAGE_CONFIG`.

For the Java client, select `--client java`. The Python configuration uses `timeout` in seconds and `custom_headers`; the Java configuration uses `timeoutInMillis` and `headers`. Both select HTTP, the original lineage endpoint, gzip, bearer API-key authentication, and `X-OpenLineage-Workspace` with the original workspace ID. That header survives a server restart and rejects an accidentally substituted workspace.

Use `--compression identity` for an uncompressed client. Produce a new settings file from the observed connection when the host address or port changes. The server instance ID belongs to operator reconnect handling; it is deliberately absent from a producer configuration that continues across ordinary restarts.

The browser's **Producer intake** control shows this same endpoint, original workspace identity, active queue and server counters. It can create the same complete client settings after the operator enters the selected producer token locally. A downloaded settings file contains that selected token and belongs in the producer's private configuration.

## Acknowledgement, retries and simultaneous arrivals

The receiver acknowledges an event only after the original source, event references and operation result have been committed through the workspace's atomic writer. Concurrent producer bodies wait in that server's append queue. An unacknowledged body stays the producer's responsibility if the process or connection is lost.

The default operation ID is `intake-` followed by the SHA-256 of the unchanged wire body. A client can instead supply its stable original `Idempotency-Key`. Retrying the same bytes, source name, reference and encoding returns the original committed response with `replayed: true`. It does not advance the workspace revision again. A changed request under the same explicit operation ID returns a conflict.

Native appends select the current revision inside the original writer. They do not overwrite earlier events or reviewed editions. If a sender explicitly supplies `If-Match`, that sender's revision must still match. Browser and SDK review, edition, attachment and explicit source-import operations continue using their existing revision checks.

| Response | Meaning and continuation |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Original source and operation are committed, or this is their exact saved replay. The response includes source identity, byte metadata, counts and original revision. |
| `400` / `415` | Correct the invalid JSON, gzip, request header or unsupported media/encoding before sending that corrected request. |
| `401` / `403` | Use the selected token, host and origin. Producer credentials apply only to the native intake endpoint. |
| `409` | The workspace pin, explicit revision or existing operation identity differs. Inspect the original selection and request. |
| `413` | The wire or decoded source exceeds its configured capacity. Select an appropriate source or explicitly configure that receiving host. |
| `503` with `Retry-After: 1` | The queue or original writer is occupied. Retry the same original body. |
| `500` / interrupted response | Preserve the original body and operation ID. A retry reconciles any commit that completed before the response was lost. |

An equivalent JSON event encoded differently has a different original source identity. Canonical event identity still joins duplicate event observations, retaining every contributing source location. Recompression may therefore create another original compressed source while retaining the same logical event.

## Capacity and observation

Default producer capacity is 64 admitted requests, 128 MiB of retained wire bodies, 64 MiB per wire body, and 64 MiB of decoded content per body. Decoding happens within the serialized commit path. The SDK host's `startServer({ producerLimits })` can select explicit limits. The decoded/source ceiling is 256 MiB; the wire buffer must accommodate one maximum-size body.

A body that cannot be admitted receives retryable backpressure. The response does not claim that its source was saved. The configured byte limits cover retained wire bodies and each decoded body; parsing and immutable workspace projection also require memory.

`GET /api/producer` reports admitted, committed, replayed, rejected and failed requests, accepted wire bytes, current queue occupancy, and the last committed source and operation. These are counters for the current server instance. Complete saved sources and operation history remain in the original workspace across restarts. Use the existing `records.read` operation with the current revision and continue every returned page for durable history.

## Native client and merchant operation

The supplied `LineageClient` can send the same native producer request:

```js
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { LineageClient } from "./client.mjs";

const producer = new LineageClient(originalConnection.url, {
  token: selectedProducerToken,
  expectedWorkspaceId: originalConnection.workspaceId
});
const originalWire = await readFile("/absolute/source/events.json.gz");
const saved = await producer.emitSource(originalWire, {
  name: "events.json.gz",
  contentEncoding: "gzip"
});
```

Keep `originalWire`, its source metadata and any explicit operation ID unchanged for response-loss recovery. The client performs one original HTTP call and returns the server's saved acknowledgement.

An operator can import a compressed original through `source.import` with its complete base64 body and `contentEncoding: 'gzip'`. The original Merchant Workspace source-import tool and host-selected import-file tool accept the same encoding. They retain their explicit operation/revision and pinned input-SHA contracts.

`source.read({ id, decode: true })` returns the original base64 body and, for gzip, the verified decoded base64 body and decoded hash. The normal object/range download still returns the exact original wire file. Complete paging and export receiving remain the existing merchant operations.

## Complete customer receiving

Save the reviewed edition and use the original full workspace export. Version 2 application packages include producer reception, typed producer interfaces, decoding, private-configuration authoring and the complete operating programme. Each compressed source is re-decoded and compared with its original decoded hash and source event references during receiving.

The current receiver also accepts complete earlier version 1 application packages with their original 35-file source set. Existing uncompressed originals use their original parser during receiving; new ingress capacities do not invalidate an earlier complete source. That earlier application edition is retained as the received source. A new compressed-source workspace carries its complete version 2 application.

The tokens and producer configuration files remain outside the exported project. Reopen the received application with the receiving operator's selected host configuration and generate producer settings from its actual new connection.

Continue the complete original native producer programme with:

```sh
node /absolute/application/PRODUCER_RECEIVING.mjs \
  /absolute/original-receiving-operation/producer-intake
```

It verifies unchanged upstream fixtures, generates private Python/Java settings, receives simultaneous plain/gzip originals, exercises actual writer backpressure, saves an edition, restarts the server, reconciles the same original producer request, exports the whole application and data, and starts an independently received application. Its saved operation, wire files, request identities and prepared export support continuation in the same directory after an interrupted run.

## Original client contract

The receiving behavior follows the original [Python HTTP transport configuration](https://openlineage.io/docs/client/python/configuration/) and [Java HTTP transport configuration](https://openlineage.io/docs/client/java/configuration/), checked on 2026-10-12. The pinned Python transport used for the implementation review is [http.py at 07864a6b](https://github.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/blob/07864a6b5f5d30b878e157eba8409dda84d68d4f/client/python/src/openlineage/client/transport/http.py), Git blob `c23dfdfcad2d2b3800d887723e34c5eb1d482d05`. It emits JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`, optional gzip and bearer API-key authentication, and supports the configured custom headers. Upstream event bodies and their original license remain in this application's existing fixture inventory.

# OpenLineage operations workspace

A private, editable operations workspace for original OpenLineage events.
Receive a producer's HTTP events or import original JSON, NDJSON or gzip files,
inspect their jobs, runs and datasets, follow
the reported dependencies, save an edition, record an operator decision and
attach a complete result to the event context that explains it. Deliver that
whole workspace, including the original files and editable application, to
another operator.

The browser, command line, Node SDK and MCP tools use the same revisioned
workspace. The maintained SCF distribution adds this product to its existing
command catalog and Applications lifecycle. Its source-owned merchant provider adds
22 tools over this same original application; see [MERCHANT.md](MERCHANT.md).

## Start

Node 22 or newer is the only runtime dependency. A received application can
run directly from its own directory; there is no package installation step.

    node cli.mjs init --workspace /absolute/private/lineage --title "Data operations"
    node cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/private/lineage --port 8767

Open the printed local URL. The browser has source import, a searchable
jobs/runs/datasets inventory, original event and facet inspection, lineage,
saved editions and comparison, reasoned reviews, attached result files and
complete downloads. Existing projects reopen through the same command.

In the maintained installed distribution:

    starforge openlineage init --workspace /absolute/private/lineage
    starforge openlineage serve --workspace /absolute/private/lineage
    starforge registrations --source openlineage-workspace

Applications lists **OpenLineage operations**. Select the initialized or
received workspace and an optional private token file, then use the existing
Review, Save, Review Start, Start, Open and Stop controls. The adapter binds the
original workspace identity and selected source to that existing lifecycle.

## Import original events

Select a complete source file in the browser or use:

    node cli.mjs import --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
      --input /absolute/producer/events.ndjson \
      --source https://your-producer.example/retained-job-log \
      --operation-id producer-capture-20261012

The CLI infers the current revision unless --revision is supplied. Reuse the
same operation ID and exact original arguments after an interrupted response.
A new intended source import gets its own ID.

Import accepts one JSON event, an array of JSON events, or NDJSON. Every
original source byte is retained under its SHA-256. Logical events deduplicate
by canonical complete event content; later observations with changed facets
remain distinct even when their run and event type match. The source inspector
retains the original source position and diagnostic for each event.

The source URL is an operator-supplied provenance field. The application does
not fetch it. Source downloads return the exact retained bytes.

### Producer HTTP transport

Native Python, Java, Airflow and other OpenLineage HTTP clients can send their
original bodies to:

    POST http://127.0.0.1:8767/api/v1/lineage

The receiver accepts uncompressed or gzip JSON/NDJSON. It retains compressed
wire bytes unchanged and verifies their decoded byte identity. Native producer
arrivals use the original workspace writer through a serial append queue.
A response acknowledges the source only after its original operation is saved.

The optional Idempotency-Key header selects the original operation ID. By
default it is derived from the unchanged wire body. Repeat the exact body,
name, reference and encoding after a lost response. An explicitly supplied
If-Match retains its numeric revision check. Queue or writer backpressure
returns 503 with Retry-After: 1.

Use the browser's **Producer intake** control to inspect the actual endpoint,
current queue and server counters and download complete Python or Java client
settings. The CLI's producer-config command creates the same private
configuration from the actual connection.json. A separate producer token can
admit events while the operator token controls the whole workspace.

[PRODUCERS.md](PRODUCERS.md) covers complete client setup, authentication, gzip,
source inspection, retries, capacity and the native producer receiving journey.

The explicit operator import route, /api/sources?name=events.ndjson&source=URL,
keeps its normal revision checks. It also accepts Content-Encoding: gzip.
To import a compressed original directly through the CLI, add
--content-encoding gzip to the import command and retain the .gz filename.

## Operate the project

1. Import complete producer files. Inspect any source diagnostics before
   choosing the event set to review.
2. Open a job, dataset or run. Namespaces are part of identity. Runs retain their
   native UUID plus the owning job identity. Inspect original facets and input
   and output observations alongside the graph.
3. Save a named edition. It retains the current event IDs and source IDs; later
   imports do not change that saved selection.
4. Compare two editions, or a saved edition with the live project. Inspect
   added events and changed jobs, datasets and run outcomes.
5. Save a review against selected entities. A reason is required. Decisions are
   accepted, needs-work, excluded or observed. Updating a review retains its
   previous text, selection and decision in the review's history.
6. Attach the complete existing result file to its saved edition and entities.
   Keep its source reference and, where applicable, its original query alongside
   the bytes. CSV, JSON, reports and other file formats remain their original
   files.
7. Export the complete workspace or generate its complete JSON, CSV or printable
   HTML report. Reopen the delivered workspace to continue the same history.

A review records a human or agent assessment. It does not erase an event,
rewrite the upstream pipeline outcome or cause an upstream job to run.
Result attachment carries existing bytes and their declared relationship to
the selected context.

## Deliver and receive

    node cli.mjs export --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
      --out /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json

The package contains the saved state, all source and attached-result objects,
and the complete portable application. Each object and application file has
its byte length and SHA-256; the complete payload has its own digest. Existing
workspace, event, edition, review and operation identities survive receiving.

    node cli.mjs verify --input /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json
    node cli.mjs receive --input /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json \
      --out /absolute/private/received-lineage
    node /absolute/private/received-lineage/application/cli.mjs serve \
      --workspace /absolute/private/received-lineage --port 8768

Receiving verifies the complete package before creating the destination. Use a
new destination directory. It restores exact original objects and reconstructs
event/source relationships from those original files, installs the included
application, and records a separate local installation ID in received.json.
Starting that received application is the explicit subsequent command.

Remote clients can download an existing export in exact, resumable byte ranges:

    import { LineageClient } from "./client.mjs";
    import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
    import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

    const client = new LineageClient("http://127.0.0.1:8767");

Keep the operation ID and exact arguments before sending a mutation if another
process will need to resume it. A 409 with the current revision means another
writer changed the project; read that change before issuing a new operation.
A replay with the same ID and original input returns the original result.

For a host-selected connection, the client supports expectedWorkspaceId and
instanceId. The server verifies these headers on the same request that performs

SOURCE_CONTRACT.md records the supported upstream schema versions, lifecycle,

with diagnostics. Native event timestamps order projections; source arrival
sequence resolves ties.

This workspace distinguishes declared job structure from individual run
observations. It follows explicit producer lineage when available and retains
the dataset-to-run-to-dataset graph when only input/output observations exist.

## Recovery and operation

The selected workspace directory holds workspace.json, content-addressed
objects/, immutable exports/, the current connection.json and a short-lived
writer.lock. Files created by the application use private permissions.

Only one mutation writes the saved state at a time. State updates use a
synchronized temporary file followed by an atomic rename. Stable operation IDs
make a lost success response recoverable. A process interruption may leave its
writer.lock. Read that original record and use:

    node cli.mjs recover-lock --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
      --id ORIGINAL_LOCK_ID

The recovery command checks that the exact original lock remains and that its
process no longer exists.

The default HTTP body limit is 64 MiB. The native producer queue has separate
wire and decoded capacity settings described in PRODUCERS.md. Direct source
imports have a 256 MiB wire/decoded ceiling, subject to available memory and disk. This first
implementation keeps the saved event index in memory for projection and writes
its JSON state atomically. Use a workspace per operational scope when the full
event history outgrows the available host.

The default listener is local to this computer. To bind another interface,
provide a private token file containing at least 24 characters. The server
rejects other browser origins, requires that token on its data routes and uses
the selected host consistently. Transport through a configured HTTPS service
is the operator's deployment responsibility.

# Original OpenLineage source contract

This application reads original OpenLineage events and retains their complete
source documents. Its operational projection has named, versioned adapters.
The original event and facet bytes remain the source of truth for further
producer-specific interpretation.

## Supported core versions

| Core version | Operational event kinds | Original schema |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1-0-1 | RunEvent | https://openlineage.io/spec/1-0-1/OpenLineage.json |
| 1-0-5 | RunEvent | https://openlineage.io/spec/1-0-5/OpenLineage.json |
| 2-0-2 | RunEvent, JobEvent, DatasetEvent | https://openlineage.io/spec/2-0-2/OpenLineage.json |

The adapter reads the original HTTPS schema origin, version and event-kind
fragment. The 1-0-1 RunEvent fragment uses /definitions/RunEvent; 1-0-5 uses
/$defs/RunEvent. The maintained upstream fluentd event_full.json declares
1-0-5 with the older /definitions/RunEvent fragment. The application retains
that exact declaration and names its compatibility interpretation
core-1-0-5-legacy-run-pointer in the original event record.

The adapters check the operational fields used for identity, chronology,
boundaries and facet projection: eventTime with a timezone, producer and
schemaURL URIs, namespaced job/dataset identities, native UUID run IDs,
declared lifecycle states, arrays of source datasets, and facet producer/schema
metadata. They retain other upstream and custom properties unchanged in each
parsed original event. A custom facet can be inspected without an installed
semantic graph adapter.

The operational adapter is explicit about the versions and fields it interprets.
Full arbitrary custom-facet JSON Schema evaluation belongs to the producer's
declared schema and is not performed by this dependency-free reader. Unsupported
or malformed operational events remain available with intake diagnostics and
their exact source file.

Official source:
https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/object-model/
https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/facets/

## Original identity and event order

A job or dataset is identified by its exact namespace and name. A run keeps
its native UUID together with the owning job namespace and name. Repeated UUIDs
under different jobs remain separate observations and produce a diagnostic.

Logical event identity is the SHA-256 of its complete canonical JSON value.
This permits a repeated original event in more than one source document while
preserving every source position. It does not collapse all events for a run,
or all events having the same lifecycle state.

Projection follows eventTime, including sub-millisecond fractional ordering,
then original intake sequence for ties. The workspace retains original
timestamps; it does not replace them with local receiving time.

Each source has a SHA-256 over its exact original wire bytes. Uncompressed
sources retain their original UTF-8 document. Gzip sources retain the compressed
request or file, contentEncoding, decodedBytes and decodedSha256. Their decoded
JSON/NDJSON goes through the same versioned parser. Array sources retain
zero-based member indexes; NDJSON sources retain one-based physical line
numbers. Blank NDJSON lines do not alter the remaining physical positions.
Original source downloads return the wire bytes. source.read with decode:true
also returns verified decoded bytes for a gzip original.

## Run lifecycle and metadata supplements

The current core makes eventType optional. When present, the adapter uses the
states declared by that version. START records the first start; COMPLETE,
FAIL and ABORT retain the original first terminal outcome and its timestamp.
A subsequent conflicting lifecycle observation stays in the event history
and adds a run issue. OTHER contributes metadata without resetting the outcome
or duration. A run lacking a lifecycle state remains OBSERVED.

JobType emissionPattern metadata is retained. COMPLETE_SNAPSHOT observations
replace the reported run boundary set; ordinary accumulative observations merge
new input/output identities. OTHER remains a metadata supplement. STREAMING or
SERVICE metadata does not imply that the absence of COMPLETE is a failed run.

Run-specific inputFacets and outputFacets stay with their original run
observations. They do not become global dataset facets.

## Facets and lineage

A later observation of a same-named facet replaces that facet's complete value.
The application does not recursively merge old nested facet fields into a new
producer declaration. A JobFacet or DatasetFacet with _deleted removes that
facet from the relevant current selection while the original event remains
inspectable.

JobEvent declarations remain a distinct job-level input/output structure.
RunEvent observations retain their own run boundaries. A later static job event
does not rewrite the inputs and outputs of an earlier run.

The explicit lineage adapter reads:

- LineageJobFacet entries from the original 1-0-0 LineageFacet schema.
- LineageDatasetFacet inputs and fields for the facet's owning dataset.
- Typed JOB and DATASET references, including a JOB's optional native runId.
- Field inputs, source field names, target field names, transformations, and
  complete original field metadata.
- The maintained ColumnLineageDatasetFacet family as a fallback when an
  explicit lineage declaration for that scope and target is absent.

A JOB reference without namespace/name uses the enclosing job as defined by
the facet. Empty explicit inputs remain an explicit absence of upstream
dependencies. Explicit facet replacement and deletion remove the superseded
relationships from the active graph. observedEdges retains the original
per-event relationship history.

When only event input/output arrays exist, the graph retains dataset-to-run
and run-to-dataset observations. It does not derive a dataset-to-dataset
Cartesian product. Where a run or job carries explicit lineage, its contextual
input/output boundaries remain separately available without allowing traversal
through those boundaries to invent extra dependencies. The lineage response
includes exact source event, facet path, schema and transformation context.

Official explicit facet:
https://openlineage.io/spec/facets/1-0-0/LineageFacet.json
https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/facets/job-facets/lineage/

## Saved editions, reviews and results

An edition captures the original source IDs and logical event IDs currently
present. Later intake leaves those identities unchanged. Edition comparison
reports added/removed/changed entity definitions and added original events.

Reviews record a decision and reason against original entity keys and,
optionally, a saved edition. Review revisions preserve the prior review record.
An attached result requires a real saved edition, existing entity selection,
complete file bytes and a source reference. Original result bytes are addressed
by SHA-256. The source reference and query explain the intended relationship;
the application does not infer a missing upstream execution from an attachment.

## Receiving

The receiver verifies the package payload and each complete object. It parses
every original source again to reconstruct event order, schema interpretation,
member positions and source references. Supplied indexes must agree with those
original bytes. Each edition's event membership must match its original selected
sources. Reviews and results must reference entities that exist in their selected
edition.

The export includes the entire portable application. Current packages declare
applicationVersion 2 and contain all 40 portable files, including the producer
queue, encoding adapter, typed producer configuration and complete operating
guides. Receiving still accepts the original 35-file application package without
applicationVersion. A gzip source requires the current application.

Receiving checks a compressed source's unchanged object hash, decoded length
and decoded hash before reconstructing its original event positions. It verifies
the complete declared application and installs it into application/; it preserves
workspace history and records a new local installation identity. Start the
application explicitly with its included CLI.

Hashes establish complete-byte identity and internal consistency. Source
origin is recorded through the supplied producer/source metadata and original
repository pins.

"""Wherobots job operations and complete data receiving."""

__version__ = "1.0.0"

// MIT. Shared ceiling for replayable native HTTP request bytes.
export const MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;

"""SF81 trusted POSIX host: pipe SF31 intent to the unchanged SF62 operator.

Default review and response use the controlling TTY. The trusted browser host
can select a framed pipe review with an exact native-request-digest decision.
This subprocess is an integration boundary, NOT a sandbox against its parent.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sys

# Capability discovery runs before SF62 is imported. It consumes no intent or
# operator arguments and never opens private keys, policy, ledger, TTY or socket.
_CAPABILITIES = {
    'schema': 'stellar-forge.sf81.capabilities.v1',
    'review_channels': ['terminal', 'pipe'],
    'review_schema': 'stellar-forge.sf81.review.v1',
    'decision_schema': 'stellar-forge.sf81.decision.v1',
    'approval_schema': 'stellar-forge.sf81.approval.v1',
    'operator_review_schema': 'stellar-forge.sf62.operator-review.v1',
}
if __name__ == '__main__' and sys.argv[1:] == ['--capabilities']:
    print(json.dumps(_CAPABILITIES, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True),
          flush=True)
    raise SystemExit(0)

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'sf62-human-approval-cli'))
from console import (Denied, ReservationApprovalDenied,  # noqa: E402
                     buyer_intent_to_governor_request, check_ledger_path,
                     reserve_interactive, reserve_reviewed)


def unique_object(pairs: list[tuple]) -> dict:
    result = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise Denied('DUPLICATE_JSON_KEY')
        result[key] = value
    return result


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, epilog=(
        'Read-only helper capabilities: --capabilities alone. '
        'This query opens no operator state.'))
    parser.add_argument('--actor', required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--service', required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--policy', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--ledger', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--review-channel', choices=('terminal', 'pipe'), default='terminal')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        raw = (sys.stdin.buffer.readline(65_538).rstrip(b'\n')
               if args.review_channel == 'pipe' else sys.stdin.buffer.read(65_537))
        if len(raw) > 65_536:
            raise Denied('INTENT_TOO_LARGE')
        def nonfinite(_):
            raise Denied('NONFINITE_JSON')
        intent = json.loads(raw.decode('utf-8'), object_pairs_hook=unique_object,
                            parse_constant=nonfinite)
        request = buyer_intent_to_governor_request(intent, actor=args.actor,
                                                   service=args.service)
        input_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
        check_ledger_path(args.ledger)
        # Serialize interactive users of this ledger, including other processes.
        # Never follow a preplaced symlink for the lock and never hold SQLite
        # transaction locks while waiting for a person.
        os.umask(0o077)
        lock_path = args.ledger.with_name(args.ledger.name + '.sf81.lock')
        fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'a') as lock:
            try:
                fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
            except BlockingIOError as exc:
                raise Denied('OPERATOR_BUSY') from exc
            if args.review_channel == 'pipe':
                def confirm(presented: dict) -> str | None:
                    print(json.dumps({'schema': 'stellar-forge.sf81.review.v1',
                        'input_sha256': input_digest, **presented},
                        separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True), flush=True)
                    line = sys.stdin.buffer.readline(4097)
                    if not line.endswith(b'\n') or len(line) > 4096:
                        raise Denied('OPERATOR_DECISION_FRAME_INVALID')
                    decision = json.loads(line.decode('utf-8'),
                        object_pairs_hook=unique_object, parse_constant=nonfinite)
                    if (type(decision) is not dict or set(decision) !=
                            {'schema', 'input_sha256', 'request_sha256', 'decision'} or
                            decision.get('schema') != 'stellar-forge.sf81.decision.v1' or
                            decision.get('input_sha256') != input_digest or
                            decision.get('request_sha256') != presented['review']['request_sha256'] or
                            decision.get('decision') not in ('approve', 'reject')):
                        raise Denied('OPERATOR_DECISION_MISMATCH')
                    return decision['request_sha256'] if decision['decision'] == 'approve' else None

                native = reserve_reviewed(intent, request, policy_path=args.policy,
                    ledger_path=args.ledger, confirm_review=confirm)
            else:
                # Separate streams avoid seeking/buffering surprises on a terminal.
                with open('/dev/tty', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as answer, \
                        open('/dev/tty', 'w', encoding='utf-8', buffering=1) as review:
                    with redirect_stdout(review):
                        native = reserve_interactive(intent, request,
                            policy_path=args.policy, ledger_path=args.ledger,
                            terminal=answer)
        print(json.dumps({'schema': 'stellar-forge.sf81.approval.v1',
            'input_sha256': input_digest, 'reservation': native},
            separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True), flush=True)
        return 0
    except (Denied, ReservationApprovalDenied, OSError, ValueError, TypeError,
            KeyError, UnicodeError, RecursionError) as exc:
        # No secrets or input content in pipe errors. A lost result after a
        # successful reserve must NEVER be reported as proof of no reservation.
        print(json.dumps({'schema': 'stellar-forge.sf81.approval.v1',
            'outcome': 'NO_APPROVAL_RETURNED', 'error_type': type(exc).__name__,
            'reason': str(exc)[:256] if isinstance(exc, (Denied, ReservationApprovalDenied))
                      else 'LOCAL_INPUT_IO_OR_TERMINAL_ERROR'}),
            flush=True)
        return 2


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Publish retained Analysis work to OpenLineage

The existing Analysis workspace can review a completed import, query, complete query export or workbook and publish its retained lineage through the original OpenLineage producer. The operator freezes the exact event bytes and destination workspace before sending. The original Analysis job owns the publication, including local cancellation, an interrupted response, same-request continuation and the accepted collector receipt.

Open the **Lineage** link in Analysis. The page is part of the same numeric-loopback server and uses its existing capability. It preserves the original Research, response-mapping, dataset, query, workbook, synthesis and backup operations.

## What the publication means

A publication describes work that already completed in the selected Analysis workspace. It reads the original records and verified files. Reviewing or publishing lineage does not rerun a query, import, purchase, model or workbook.

| Original completed operation | Projected input and output |
| --- | --- |
| Dataset import or response import | Exact retained source-manifest digest to the original immutable SQLite version. The original import/preview identity and incomplete-response acknowledgement remain visible. |
| Query | Actual native read tables and their immutable versions to the saved query preview. Its result digest, saved row count and truncated flag distinguish that preview from a complete export. |
| Query export | The original reviewed query and source bindings to the complete native export. The original export reader verifies the retained files, SQL, parameters, view selection and manifest. Its own completed read transaction supplies the actual read tables and immutable source-version records. Its data inputs are the immutable versions, not the preview rows. |
| Workbook | Actual retained query-export or report-publication sources to the workbook revision, definition, sheet mappings and files. Original report-publication identity is retained; this producer does not invent its internal ancestors. |

Each included completed job supplies a START and COMPLETE event using its original recorded timestamps. The events explicitly mark this retrospective projection. Run IDs are the original 32-character job IDs in UUID notation. Dataset names use original immutable version, query, export and workbook IDs inside the original Analysis workspace namespace.

The reviewer sees source and output hashes, actual row scope, source mappings, known dependencies and any missing or ambiguous earlier writer. A version imported outside the retained Analysis jobs can still be an exact source dataset. It does not acquire an invented Analysis import run.

The default outbound source contains operational metadata, column names and digests. It excludes parameter values and result rows. **Include original SQL text** adds the original SQL only when explicitly selected. The full local handover retains native job requests/results and source manifests, so the review and its recorded provenance can be reconstructed.

## Configure an original collector

Use the existing OpenLineage workspace and its producer endpoint. The original application lives at:

Select the original collector's saved `connection.json` file. It contains the actual `commons.openlineage.startup.v1` identity, including its workspace ID, current instance ID and URL. The Analysis connection pins the workspace ID. It reads the current saved startup file for every attempt. A restarted instance can change its port on the same numeric-loopback host and protocol while preserving the same publication. A changed scheme, hostname or non-loopback origin is rejected before dispatch and requires a newly reviewed destination. An unresolved publication should first be reconciled at its original destination. The bridge checks the actual startup-file URL again, so a file change between local preparation and dispatch cannot change this destination policy.

The bridge requires a caller-owned token file without group/other permission bits on Unix. Request files are created by the original private Analysis storage helpers.

The collector profile is optional. Saved plans, receipts and handovers remain readable with no configured collector or Node runtime.

## Review, freeze and publish

1. Choose an original completed operation. The list is paginated; an exact retained job ID can also be entered.
2. Review the verified dependency closure. Inspect the jobs, input/output datasets, original timestamps, query-preview scope, complete output manifests and source warnings.
3. Select the named collector and record the review title/note. Decide explicitly whether to include SQL text.
4. Freeze the review. Analysis captures the original native records again and requires the exact reviewed snapshot digest. The resulting plan contains immutable event bytes, source SHA-256, target workspace ID and original producer key.
5. Publish the saved source. Analysis retains one original job ID for this plan before dispatch.
6. Read the native receipt. The page keeps collector revision, added/retained event counts, source identity, replay status and actual endpoint separate from local attempt status.

The source name is `analysis-lineage-<plan-id>.json`. Its original key is `analysis-<analysis-workspace-id>-<plan-id>`. A retry uses the same source name, source URL, bytes and key. Another publication job cannot be substituted for an already-admitted plan.

The browser saves its exact plan and publication requests before POST. A lost browser reply is reconciled by reading the original saved plan/job. If the request was not admitted, the explicit continuation uses the same retained body. A new browser can reopen a plan from server history and follow its original publication job without the old browser journal.

## Interrupted and cancelled attempts

The original Runtime and Node bridge own one attempt from file verification through final reply publication. They use the original client's HTTP status, error details and `Retry-After` header.

| Retained observation | Operator action |
| --- | --- |
| NOT_STARTED | Correct the original runtime/configuration admission issue, then continue the same job. |
| NOT_DISPATCHED | The bridge proved the HTTP send had not begun. Correct its exact source/configuration issue and continue the same request. |
| HTTP_REJECTED | A complete native response with a documented preflight 4xx status proves rejection. Read the actual status and continue the original key after correcting that condition. |
| OUTCOME_UNKNOWN | The send may have committed before the reply was lost, incomplete, invalid or followed by a 5xx response. An invalid 2xx acknowledgement is also unknown. Continue the same source/key so the original producer returns its retained replay result. |
| ACCEPTED | Preserve the complete receipt. A later local timeout/cancellation does not undo the collector acknowledgement. |

**Stop this local attempt** signals the current native operation and retains that cancellation request. It does not remove events from the collector. The same publication remains explicitly resumable. The application does not automatically retry a stopped or failed request.

On workspace reopen, an existing complete validated acceptance restores the corresponding original job's completed state. Otherwise an interrupted job remains visible for explicit continuation. The collector's original idempotency behavior resolves a committed send whose acknowledgement was lost.

Closing Analysis drains its owned lineage operations through receipt publication and local cleanup. Disposable credential-reference files are removed only after an outcome is retained. If local receipt publication fails, the original request/log files remain in the private attempt directory for recovery.

## Source and decision identities

manifest SHA-256, selected source columns, public aliases and representations.

read by that completed export. A preview row count is never used as the complete
dataset size.

revision. Repeating that ID and body reopens the saved decision before requiring
the source files to be available again. A changed selection is a newly reviewed
recipe revision.

A dataset-package job streams every original typed row. The complete manifest is
published after the data and descriptor. A same-ID continuation verifies any
already-complete files and finishes missing derived outputs.

Each native source/publisher action is a dataset-source job. It retains the
original request, reviewed connection, prepared package index and deterministic
native request UUID before dispatch. The Node bridge uses the original

## Prepare the source in the browser

1. Use the existing Analysis full query-export workflow. Select a COMPLETE export
   with queryComplete true and the original typed rows.jsonl file.
2. Open Dataset publication and inspect its original IDs, raw manifest hash, full
   row count and typed preview.
3. Select the public fields explicitly; the first form selects none.
4. Set each public alias and representation. Reorder the selected fields when
   their public order matters.
5. Enter a package/resource name, public title and private rights/scope note.
   Select a license only when it is authorized for those values.
6. Save the reviewed recipe and prepare that exact saved revision.
7. Inspect its public files, private manifest/report and measured field statistics.

Public aliases begin with a letter and contain only letters, digits or
underscores, up to 48 characters. The names constructor, prototype and __proto__
are rejected. Private recipe names have a saved revision; public package/resource
names are lowercase identifiers.

### Representations

| Selection | Original value | Published value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| text | String or SQL null | Exact string or JSON null |
| integer | Integer within ±(2^53−1), or null | Exact safe JSON integer or null |
| number | Safe integer or finite float, or null | JSON number or null; negative floating zero is rejected |
| boolean01 | Integer 0/1, or null | JSON false/true or null |
| integer-text | Original integer, or null | Exact decimal text or null |
| sqlite-json | Original encoded SQLite scalar | A JSON string containing that canonical encoded value |
| base64 | Original encoded SQLite blob, or null | Canonical Base64 text or null |

No string is parsed as a number, timestamp or Boolean because of its spelling.
Exact decimal strings remain text when the text representation is selected.

The sqlite-json representation preserves distinctions within an explicit JSON
string. SQL null becomes the text null, an empty string becomes the JSON text
for an empty string, and an original string saying null stays a quoted string.
The original tagged binary/nonfinite encodings are preserved in that text.

A mismatch fails at its actual original row and column. The retained error
identifies row, source column, output alias and representation without copying
the private cell. Review a new recipe revision to choose another representation;
do not change an accepted preparation request.

### Standards and public scope

The descriptor uses the general **data-package** profile and a **data-resource**
with an explicit Table Schema. Its external resource is data.json. The v1
Tabular Data Resource profile permits only CSV for non-inline resources, so this
external JSON is not labeled with that profile.

Table Schema missingValues is empty. The descriptor preserves field order,
representation metadata, resource byte length and SHA-256. An operator-selected
primary key is declared for the native workbench to review; this serializer
does not introduce a second primary-key validator.

Official references:

- https://specs.frictionlessdata.io/data-package/
- https://specs.frictionlessdata.io/data-resource/
- https://specs.frictionlessdata.io/tabular-data-resource/
- https://specs.frictionlessdata.io/table-schema/

| File | Scope | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| datapackage.json | Public | Selected metadata, Table Schema and stable provenance IDs/hashes |
| data.json | Public | Every selected row in its reviewed representation |
| publication.zip | Public | Exactly the two public files above |
| recipe.json | Private | Complete reviewed selection and rights note |
| manifest.json | Private | Full native binding, recipe, file hashes and measured field statistics |
| report.html | Private | Human-readable source and package review |

The public descriptor excludes SQL, parameter text, private paths, tokens and the
rights note. Public title, description, license and selected values are
intentionally public. The public ZIP never includes the private handover files.

The data-file ceiling is explicitly selected, up to 256 MiB. The example defaults
to 64 MiB. Browser downloads buffer and verify at most 64 MiB per file. The CLI
streams the same retained files when they are larger.
